## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want tests that pin how scaled enemy counts reach the campaign (static and sequenced) without breaking determinism or the existing campaign invariants, so the density change cannot silently reshape the authored campaign.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Enemy counts rise with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Add tests (in the existing wave test files, or a new `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts`) that:

- Assert level-1 `LEVELS` wave groups are unchanged by the scaling path (deep-equal counts), so onboarding data stays byte-identical.
- Assert a level-10 group grows by the documented multiplier with the documented rounding, floor of 1, 200-per-group cap, and `single`-formation groups remain exactly 1.
- Assert the scaling is applied to **both** the static `LEVELS` campaign and the sequenced campaign (`buildSequencedLevels`, covering `fixed`, `curve` and `dynamic` generation modes), through the shared build seam.
- Assert same-seed builds remain byte-identical (determinism contract) and that a second build of the same campaign is idempotent (no double scaling).
- Assert the scaled campaign still satisfies the existing invariants and wave-balance rules: `campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `campaignRoster.test.ts`, `waveBalance` R1–R3, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`.
- Assert the shared helper is the only scaling implementation consumed by game and gym launch paths (parity seam), not a duplicated copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD for the specified reason (no scaling applied/nonexistent helper).
- Tests cover level-1 identity, level-10 growth, rounding, floor, cap, `single` groups, both campaign paths, same-seed determinism and no double scaling.
- Tests cover scaled-campaign compliance with the existing campaign invariants and wave-balance rules.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/waves/Formations.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- optionally `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts` (new)
- existing invariant suites: `src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `src/core/waveBalance.test.ts`

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules" (needs the helper contract). Blocks the campaign count-application feature.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want deterministic tests that prove the kill-time power-up supply falls with the campaign level, so the supply curve cannot regress unnoticed.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Power-up supply per enemy falls with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Extend `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (and the rules tests where appropriate) with tests that:

- Force the scene RNG so the number of drops over N kills is exact and deterministic at level 1 (matches the current 0.18 rate) and at level 10 (matches 0.05, i.e. at most 30 % of the level-1 rate).
- Prove the level is resolved from the live campaign (`WaveManager.currentLevel()?.level`), i.e. after advancing a level the next kills use the new chance, and an unknown level falls back to level 1.
- Prove the small-asteroid Extra Life roll scales by the same ratio and is unchanged at level 1 (`rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`).
- Prove drop types/weights, the mineral kill-drop rule and timed weapon/power-up effects are unaffected.

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (flat 0.18 roll for every level).
- Assertions are exact and seeded — no statistical/threshold flakiness.
- Coverage includes level 1 identity, level 10 endpoint, mid-run level advance, unknown-level fallback and Extra Life proportionality.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Goal (user story)

As a ring-timing harness operator, I want every metric line of `formatRingTimingReport` to describe the seed set (not seed 1's sample), so the text report and the JSON artefact agree.

## Summary

`formatRingTimingReport` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from `report.runs[0]` (seed 1) while every other line uses the summary means. Add the missing aggregate stats to `RingTimingSummary`, render from the summary, and regenerate the committed artefact so its JSON summary carries the new fields.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `RingTimingSummary` gains `betweenSortieMinutes`, `retryMinutes`, `retakeMinutes` and `expectedRetakes` as `RingTimingStats` (count/mean/min/max), populated in `simulateRingTiming` via `stats(runs.map(...))`.
- `formatRingTimingReport` renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from the summary aggregates (mean, with min-max where the JSON summary carries them) - never from `report.runs[0]`; a single-seed report still renders that seed's figures under its `seed 1` header.
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` is regenerated (`npm run ring-timing -- --json --out docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, default rings/lines/seeds 1-3): deterministic, so every existing mean/min/max value is unchanged and the summary merely gains the four new fields; the committed-evidence tests still pass.
- The sibling pinning test (AH-0MWGVXB95002W7KI) passes; the full project test suite passes via the test skill at the dev-push gate.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the `RingTimingSummary` interface and its construction in `simulateRingTiming`.
- Update the three lines of `formatRingTimingReport` to read `summary.*.mean` (min-max where carried), mirroring the `total` line's style.
- Regenerate the committed artefact via the CLI; update the fixture type `CommittedBaselineReport` only if its partial shape needs extending (it already tolerates extra keys).
- Verify via `/skill:test` (never ad-hoc test commands): changed-scope gate, then the committed-evidence suite / full gate.

- Reporting/consistency fix only: no behaviour or measured-value changes; the regenerated artefact's existing totals must be byte-identical in value.
- Additive JSON arity: no exported `RingTimingSummary` field is renamed or removed.
- UK English.

## Risky assumptions

- Regeneration is deterministic (asserted by the existing determinism test): same seeds/options reproduce identical values, so committed totals cannot drift. Success threshold: the regenerated artefact's existing mean/min/max are unchanged.

# Tests: bot-upgrade fit-rule and purchase-economics contract (red-first)

Child of AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ (Strengthen a hexes defence). Red-first guard tests for the pure bot-upgrade contract — written first, RED until the `botUpgrade` module (its implementation sibling) lands. No implementation ships in this item; it pins the contract.

## Target outcome

A test-only item that locks the fit rule, the per-level upgrade price (Q9 = B), the purchase economics and the one-formula rating recompute so the pure module can be implemented (TDD) against a fixed contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fit-rule tests assert every authored verdict against `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`: `upgrade-existing` (the bot already carries the weapon → its level rises by one), `add-to-empty-slot` (a weapon kind the bot does not carry → offered **only** when at least one permanent slot is free), `re-hull` (a hull entry), `train` (a modifier entry whose effect changes stored defender data), and each disabled reason (slot pool full / unaffordable in either currency / ring-gated).

# Purchase seeds the level-1 row and the upgrade rule reads the owned set

## Purpose

Close the reported bug: a purchase must create the power-up's **first permanent
level row** (producer Q2 = (ii), A3), so the existing buy-to-upgrade rule offers
a next level and the deploy grant hands the level to the run. Both the owned set
and the seeded row land in **one** payload write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buy` seeds `hangar.powerUpLevels` with `{ id, level: 1 }` for a power-up
  purchase in the same returned hangar that carries the ownership entry and the
  spent currency, so `purchaseHangarEntry`'s one `saveHangarWarPayload` write
  persists both fields together — a saved purchase can never own a power-up
  without its level, or the reverse.
- A refused purchase seeds no row, adds no ownership entry and spends nothing.
- `ownsUpgradeableKind` reads a power-up as owned from `hangar.unlockedPowerUps`
  **union** a persisted `powerUpLevels` row (a row written by an older save still
  implies ownership, so no stored row is orphaned); there is no third
  representation and no ownership check outside `ownedIds`/`ownsUpgradeableKind`.
- An unowned power-up is still refused `unowned`; the just-purchased one offers
  and buys its next level through `hangarWarStore.buyHangarUpgrade`
  (`upgradeHangarKind`), raising the level by exactly one with `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL`
  as the single ceiling (level 1 after purchase leaves four purchasable steps).
- The chain purchase → seeded row → upgrade → deploy is proven end to end:
  `buildHangarDeployment` carries the bought and raised levels in
  `HangarWarDeployment.powerUpLevels`, and `applyHangarWarDeployment` grants them
  onto the run `Player`.
- The `hangarEconomy.ts` comment calling a `powerUpLevels` row "the only place the
  hangar records a power-up level" is corrected to separate **level** from
  **ownership** (ownership = `unlockedPowerUps`), matching the persisted
  contract's documentation.
- The red-first assertions owned by this slice pass, including the
  `non-upgradeable` refusal for a consumable and the field-pickup-only id.

- Buying a power-up through `buy` spends its price, adds the id to
  `unlockedPowerUps` and seeds its `hangar.powerUpLevels` row at `level` 1 in one
  payload write, so the deploy grant sees it on the very next deployment; a
  refused purchase changes neither field and spends nothing.
- `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` read power-up ownership from `unlockedPowerUps`
  (a persisted level row also implies ownership); an unowned power-up is still
  refused `unowned`, the purchased one offers and buys the next level through the
  store's `buyHangarUpgrade`, and the deploy path grants the raised level onto the
  run `Player`.

## Minimal Implementation

- Seed the row inside the pure `buy` (one place, next to the owned-set push),
  reusing the existing row vocabulary rather than a new helper or a second write.
- Change `ownsUpgradeableKind`'s power-up branch to
  `hangar.unlockedPowerUps.includes(id) || levels.powerUps.some(...)`; leave the
  weapon branch and every refusal class untouched.
- Add no new store function: `buyHangarUpgrade`, `withPermanentLevels` and
  `hangarPermanentLevels` already carry the row through the payload.
- Leave the UI affordance untouched — `buildUpgradeAffordance` is id-driven, so
  the owned row's `UPGRADE` state comes from the shared renderer.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the catalogue-kind / owned-set slice. Blocks the docs slice.

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`

- The seeded level-1 row, the union ownership read, the corrected comment and the
  end-to-end purchase → upgrade → deploy tests.

## Purpose

  `isPurchasableEntry` in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) is the **single**
  definition of "the bot may shop this", and it excludes the new `'power-up'`
  kind.
- `cheapestUsefulUnlock` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) and

  traversal replay produce their current results.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`'s unlock-pace numbers for the pre-existing
  catalogue entries are byte-identical; the report's new power-up rows are pinned
  explicitly in its tests (no silent total or count drift), and any doc or report

- The helper is tested both ways: a power-up entry is excluded from the bot's
  candidates while a hull / weapon / modifier entry at the same ring and price

- The exclusion rationale (the bot buys the cheapest **useful** unlock; power-ups

- The attract/traversal bot's purchase candidates keep their current kind set

# Intake brief — Hex Map Information UX (AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM)

## Headline

The Hex Map screen (`HexMapScene`) draws roughly fifteen separately positioned
text objects and a ring of tiles with **no sectioning at all**: war status,
transient "what just happened" news, the map itself, the selected hex's intel and
the controls legend all float over the same background, in three different
columns and two different font conventions. This item introduces named,
visually bounded **sections** — each with its own heading — so every group of
information is distinguishable at a glance.

## Problem statement

There is a lot of information on the Hex Map and too little structure holding it
apart. Measured against the shipped renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`,
960×540), the screen currently carries:

| What is drawn | Where it sits today |
|---|---|
| Screen title, and the run result line (`RUN: VICTORY · score N`) | centred, top (`y=18`, `y=46`) |
| Ring progress (`RING 2 — 3/12 HEXES HELD`) | left column (`x=24`, `y=62`) |
| Frontier strength (`FRONTIER · STR n · BEAT ≤ m (k IN REACH)`) | left column (`y=82`) |
| Hangar fleet + bank (`HANGAR · hull · n min · n cores`) | left column (`y=102`) |
| `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` panel (rolled-in defence report) | left column (`y=118`, conditional) |
| `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner (ring won / hangar falls) | left column (`y=300`, conditional) |
| `◀ HANGAR` action row | left column (`y=468`) |
| `READ THE MAP` legend, six lines of static help | right column (`y=112`–`y=182`) |
| `SELECTED HEX — FULL INTEL` detail panel | right column (`y=200`) |
| Hex tiles (`AGG n` + ownership marker + `(q,r)`), attack arrows, hangar marker | centre |
| Keyboard hint line | bottom centre (`y=530`) |

Three problems follow from that inventory:

1. **Unlike information is adjacent, like information is apart.** The three
   left-hand header lines mix ring progress, frontier combat maths and hangar
   inventory with no heading to separate them, while the two halves of "the
   selected hex" (its intel, right column; its attack row, left column) sit on
   opposite sides of the screen.
2. **Transient news has no home.** The run result is centred at the top, the
   hangar-assault outcome is a left-hand banner, and the banked win-bonus line
   (`model.winBonusLine`) is computed but **never drawn at all** — its only
   consumer is the `getWinBonusLine()` test seam. "What just happened" therefore
   arrives in up to three different places, one of which is nowhere.
3. **Help competes with content.** A six-line static legend occupies the top of
   the same right-hand column as the dynamic intel panel it explains, so the
   loudest text in that column is documentation rather than information about
   the player's war.

## Users

- **The Hangar War player** landing on the map between sorties.
  - *As a player, I want the map's status, my last sortie's outcome, the ring
    itself and the selected hex's intel each in their own labelled section, so I
    can find one thing without reading everything.*
  - *As a player, I want to know what just happened (victory/defeat, ring won or
    hangar falls, minerals banked) in one place, so I do not have to hunt three
    corners of the screen for the aftermath of my deployment.*
  - *As a player reading the selected hex, I want its intel and its attack row
    together, so one hex is one story rather than two panels apart.*
  - *As a colour-blind player, I want sections distinguished by headings and
    framing rather than by colour alone, consistent with the map's existing
    CVD-safe conventions.*
- **The maintainer** of the shared `buildHexMapModel` → `renderHexMap` pair,
  who needs the section layout to live in one renderer so the game and the
  `GymHexWar` parity gym cannot drift (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

## Producer decisions (2026-11-17)

- **Q1 = (a)** — sections are **bordered, headed panels** laid out in fixed
  columns; every section has a frame, a heading and a bounded rect.
- **Q2 = (b)** — **four content sections plus a controls footer**: WAR STATUS,
  LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX (intel **and** its attack row together), and
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
- **Q3 = (a)** — the banked win-bonus line **is rendered**, inside LAST SORTIE.

## Section model (producer-approved)

Four content sections plus a controls footer, each drawn as a **bordered,
headed panel** with a bounded rect:

| Section | Contains | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| `war-status` | ring progress, frontier strength / beatable ceiling / in-reach count, hangar hull + banked minerals/cores | always |
| `last-sortie` | run result line, banked win bonus, hangar-assault outcome (`RING WON…` / `HANGAR FALLS…`) | only when the landing carries one of those |
| `map` | the ring tiles, attack arrows and hangar marker | always |
| `selected-hex` | the focused hex's full intel **and** its `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` row | always (panel body may be empty when nothing is focused) |
| `controls` | keyboard hint line + the `READ THE MAP` legend | always |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Section registry on the shared view.** `HexMapView` publishes a `sections`
  list — `{ key, heading, rect }` per rendered section — and every rendered text
  object, tile and arrow lies inside **exactly one** section rect, with no two
  section rects overlapping and every rect inside the 960×540 frame.
- **Every section is a bordered, headed panel (Q1 = a).** Each of `war-status`,
  `last-sortie` (when shown), `map`, `selected-hex` and `controls` draws a panel
  frame and one heading from a shared exported constant (`WAR STATUS`,
  `LAST SORTIE`, `SELECTED HEX`, `CONTROLS`, and the map's own title), in one
  consistent style and position convention, so the groupings are distinguishable
  without relying on colour.
- **No information is lost.** Every string the current renderer draws still
  renders, in its new section; the tile labels (`AGG n`, ownership marker,
  `(q,r)`), arrows, hint line and legend text are unchanged in content.
- **Transient news is grouped and complete (Q2 = b, Q3 = a).** The run result
  line, the hangar-assault banner and the banked win-bonus line
  (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`, from `model.winBonusLine`) render **only**
  inside `last-sortie`; the win-bonus line is now actually drawn, not merely
  queryable. When the landing carries none of the three, the section is absent
  (no empty headed box).
- **One hex, one section.** The selected hex's intel and its attack row render
  inside the same `selected-hex` section; the attack row is hidden (not moved to
  another section) when the focused hex is in no attack.
- **Help no longer competes with content.** The `READ THE MAP` legend moves into
  the `controls` section and no longer occupies the intel column.
- **Legibility at 960×540.** No section body text overdraws a hex tile or the
  hangar marker; long strings (draw name, assault arithmetic) word-wrap inside
  their section; no rendered text is smaller than today's smallest (9px) and
  headings are at least 10px.
- **Game/gym parity, one shared layout.** All layout lives in
  `renderHexMap`/`hexMap.ts`; `GymHexWar` renders the same sections read-only
  through the same call, and no gym-local or scene-local layout exists (the
  existing `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions stay green).
- **Interaction contract unchanged.** Grid arrow navigation, Tab/Shift+Tab
  cycling, Enter/Space inspect-or-deploy, tile hover/click, the `◀ HANGAR` row
  and ESC-to-menu behave exactly as before; the attract traversal still takes
  exactly one next action and cannot stall on a section.
- **Regression coverage.** `HexMapScene.test.ts`, the renderer/`hexIntel` tests
  and `GymHexWar.test.ts` pin the section registry (keys, headings, non-overlap,
  in-frame), `last-sortie` visibility toggling, and that the selected-hex intel
  and attack row share a section; position-only pins may be updated, behaviour
  pins may not be weakened.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** — GDD §8.2 (the
  map's screen surface), the `hexMap.ts` module docblock, and
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` if its row description changes.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A Hangar War player can read the map at a glance: the war's status, the last
sortie's outcome, the ring itself, the selected hex's intel and the controls each
sit in their own labelled section instead of scattering across three columns.

## Constraints

- **Renderer-only change.** The model (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) stays
  the single source of every string; `hexMap.ts` only draws and positions. No
  gameplay rule, resolver call or persisted state is added.
- **One layout for game and gym.** The gym↔game parity contract and the existing
  `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions forbid a second layout implementation.
- **Single 960×540 viewport.** No scrolling, panning, tabs or collapsible
  sections unless the producer chooses the tabbed option in Q1.
- **Transient launch data stays transient** — run result, tick record, assault
  and win bonus are never persisted; a later entry renders no `last-sortie`.
- **Existing CVD-safe conventions hold** — section distinction must not depend on
  colour; the tile ownership encoding (blue/orange + filled/hollow marker) is
  untouched.
- **No new assets or fonts** — monospace text and Phaser Graphics panels only.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (951 lines) holds every layout constant
  (`PANEL_X`, `ATTACK_PANEL_Y`, `ASSAULT_BANNER_Y`, legend rows, hint line) and
  draws all of the inventory above. There is no section abstraction: each text
  object is positioned by a hand-tuned literal.
- `HexMapView` already exposes behavioural seams (`getRows`, `getArrows`,
  `getPanelText`, `getLeftPanelText`, `getAssaultText`, …) but nothing describing
  screen regions, so no test can currently assert grouping or non-overlap.
- `model.winBonusLine` exists (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` →
  `defenceReport.ts`) and is surfaced only by `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`;
  the renderer never draws it.
- Prior work already fixed the map's *readability* (reveal filter, CVD-safe tiles,
  coordinates, titled detail-panel lines) and its *navigation* (grid arrows), so
  this item is the remaining structural/visual-hierarchy step.

## Desired change

A sectioned Hex Map: a small number of named, bounded regions with headings, each
holding one kind of information, drawn by the shared renderer so the game and the
parity gym stay identical; transient sortie news gathered into one place; the
selected hex's intel and attack row brought together; help demoted to a controls
footer.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the whole layout: section rects, headings,
  legend relocation, last-sortie grouping; add `sections` to `HexMapView`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — shared section-heading constants and any
  model wiring for the last-sortie lines (`winBonusLine` is already published)
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — query seam for `sections`, transient launch data
  plumbing (no rule change)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — renders the same sections read-only
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — section/grouping pins; update
  position-only assertions
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — describe the
  sectioned map surface

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed): the
  scene and its intel model this item re-lays-out.
- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** — Hangar Map UX (completed, parent): reveal filter,
  CVD-safe ownership, coordinates on tiles, spatial arrows — the readability and
  navigation pass that precedes this structural one.
- **AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK** — Hangar Map UI: clearer overview (completed): titled
  every line of the selected-hex intel. Its line titles are load-bearing for
  this item's `selected-hex` section and must not be disturbed.
- **AH-0MWEWYUAS002P7P9** — Renderer: CVD-safe labels, reveal filter, owned-hex
  selection (completed); **AH-0MWEWYVD7008PPQT** — Navigation: grid columns
  (completed): both pin renderer behaviour this item must preserve.
- **AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP** — Defence report rolled into the hex map (completed):
  source of the attack arrows and the left-hand attack panel now moved into
  `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEZZA4E0081NJ5** — Assault defence report and reset announcement
  (completed): source of the `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner now grouped under
  `last-sortie`.
- **AH-0MWF0CWB7002MG2F** — Special-mission intel (completed): the `★ SPECIAL`
  tile tag whose detail-panel block lives in `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** — Win path: bank a fixed post-win bonus (open): owns the
  `winBonusLine` whose presentation Q3 decides.
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** — Text on hex map is unreadable (completed): the
  legibility baseline this item must not regress.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** – Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed)
- **AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU** – Player has no audio (completed)
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** – Text on hex map is unreadable (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: clearly, create, easily, group, hex, hexmap, identify, information, logical, lot, make, map, much, page, presented, sections, sense, there
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: clearly, create, distinguishable, group, hex, hexmap, lot, make, map, much, page, sections, there
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: create, group, hex, hexmap, logical, lot, make, map, much, page, presented, there

Keyword false positive: `AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU` (audio) matched on generic words
(`make`, `there`) and is not related to this item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Clutter inversion.** More framing can add more visual noise than it removes;
  mitigation: a small fixed section count (4 + footer by default), one heading
  style, and the non-overlap/fit assertions as the guard.
- **Text reflow collisions.** Wrapped draw names and long assault arithmetic are
  the strings that collide at 960×540; mitigation: wrap widths inside each
  section rect plus the "no body text overdraws a tile" assertion.
- **Parity drift.** A scene-local tweak would break gym↔game parity; mitigation:
  all layout in `hexMap.ts`, with the existing equivalence assertions kept.
- **Test churn on positions.** Several suites assert coordinates indirectly;
  mitigation: pin sections structurally (`sections` registry) rather than by
  literal pixel offsets, and update only position-only assertions.
- **Scope creep** into a full visual redesign, new fonts, or tabbed navigation;
  such opportunities are recorded as new linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** headings are monospace text in the existing style (no new
  assets); **assumption:** the attract/demo traversal gains no new state, because
  every section is read-only like today's panels.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — How should the sections be delineated?**
  (a) Bordered, headed panels in fixed columns — every section has a frame, a
  heading and a bounded rect (recommended).
  (b) Headed bands with separator rules only — headings plus horizontal rules,
  no boxes, more breathing space over the map background.
  (c) Collapsible/tabbed sections — only one section expanded at a time, cutting
  on-screen text but adding interaction state and hidden information.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a frame per section is the most unambiguous
  distinction, needs no new interaction, and is directly assertable (rect +
  heading + non-overlap) by the existing scene/renderer tests.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** bordered, headed panels in fixed
  columns. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q2 (ANSWERED, producer chose (b)) — Which grouping taxonomy should the map use?**
  (a) Six sections: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX, ATTACK,
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
  (b) Four sections plus a footer: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX
  (intel **and** its attack row together), CONTROLS/LEGEND (recommended).
  (c) Keep today's regions and only add headings/separators to each.
  **Recommended:** (b) — it separates the three genuinely unlike kinds of
  information (war state, transient news, focused-hex detail) while keeping one
  hex's intel and attack row together, and it avoids the extra section that
  option (a) spends on material that is about the same focused hex.
  Research: the inventory in *Problem statement* comes from
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`; the attack panel and the detail panel are both
  keyed by the focused hex (`model.attackDetails` / `displayedHexKey`), which is
  what makes (b) coherent.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (b)** four sections plus a controls footer,
  with the focused hex's intel and its attack row in one `selected-hex` section.
  Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q3 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — Should the banked win-bonus line be
  rendered as part of this item?**
  (a) Yes — render `model.winBonusLine` (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`) inside
  LAST SORTIE (recommended).
  (b) No — leave it query-only and record it as deliberately out of scope.
  (c) Remove the unused line/model field entirely.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the line already exists and is tested through the query
  seam; without it the "what just happened" section silently omits a reward the
  player just earned, and it is a one-line addition to a section this item is
  already building.
  Research: `winBonusLine` is produced by `defenceReport.ts` and republished by
  `hexIntel.ts`; `hexMap.ts` never draws it and `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`
  is its only reader.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** render `model.winBonusLine` inside
  `last-sortie`. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q4 (recorded, not blocking) — Is a repo/gym search needed for the selected-hex
  line titles?** Answered by inspection of AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK: the titles
  (`ID:`, `STATE:`, `BOSS:`, `STRENGTHS:`, …) are shipped and are treated as a
  fixed input here. Source: work item description + `hexIntel.ts` constants.

# Completing a hex battle means the equipped hulls/weapons/plugins are reset

## Problem statement

The hangar currently treats the **whole fleet as permanent**: a deployed ship is not consumed when a battle ends, and buying an upgrade does not arm it. The producer wants each deployed ship to be a **one-battle consumable** — the flown hull, its equipped starting weapons and modifiers, and their bought permanent levels are spent on **win or loss** — while owned items the player did not fly, and the free starter kit, survive. Re-fitting a new ship must be quick, so **buying an upgrade should enable it immediately**, and a follow-on item will add saved ship configurations for one-action re-purchase.

## Users

- **Primary — the player** building and flying ships through the hex war.
- **Secondary — the balance/progression owner**, because the salvage economy must now fund re-fitting after every sortie.

Example user stories:

- As a player, after a battle I want the ship I flew to be spent, so each sortie is a real commitment and losing one costs me the ship, not my whole collection.
- As a player, I want buying an upgrade to arm it immediately, so re-fitting a new ship takes one action per part instead of buy-then-hunt-for-equip.
- As a player, I want the owned items I did not fly to survive, so a bad run never erases my progress.
- As a player, I want to keep the free starter hull and starter weapon, so I can always deploy after a wipe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On completion of a hex deployment — **win or loss** — the deployed ship is removed from the hangar payload: the deployed hull (unless it is the free starter hull), every starting weapon in the hangar's active loadout (unless it is the free starter weapon), every modifier in that loadout, and the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows for those consumed ids are deleted. Every owned item the player did not deploy, and the free starter kit, remain owned.
- After the consumption the hangar is reset to the free starter kit: `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty, so the next deployment uses only the free starter kit until the player re-purchases. The player's `bankedMinerals` and `bankedCores` are unchanged by consumption (the existing win bonus still applies on a win).
- A successful hangar purchase **auto-enables** the entry: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, and a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers`; a refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership nor the loadout. This deliberately supersedes the economy's current "buying never equips" rule for the hangar screen, while other callers can keep the old behaviour through an explicit option.
- Automated tests cover both outcome paths and the purchase paths through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity): win and loss consumption, starter-kit survival, un-flown owned items surviving, consumed items' level rows removed, no soft-lock with an empty loadout, demo mode not overwriting the player's war, and auto-enable plus refusal for hull/weapon/modifier.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

After every hex battle the ship you flew is spent and you rebuild from the salvage you earned — and because buying an upgrade now arms it immediately, re-fitting a new ship takes fewer steps and each sortie feels like a real commitment.

## Constraints

- **No soft-lock.** The free starter hull (`hull-1`) and starter weapon (`spread`) are always owned; an empty loadout is legal (deploy with the ship's permanent cannon only, AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D).
- **One payload write per battle** through the existing `saveHangarWarPayload`; defensive parsing stays the authority; no schema-version bump expected because the shape is unchanged.
- **Demo/attract runs never overwrite the player's war** — the existing `_saveHangarWarPayload` demo guard must keep holding for the consumed payload.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The consumption rule lives in the pure core and is exercised by the headless harness; no scene-only logic.
- **Supersedes a prior decision.** `hangarEconomy.buy()` currently documents that "buying only grants ownership — equipping stays the deployment selector's job" (A5/A6). This item overrides that for the hangar screen only.
- **Separate concern left alone.** The ring-end hangar-falls reset (`resetCampaign`, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J) already wipes both axes and is unchanged.
- **No new balance tuning.** The existing win bonus (`bankWinBonus` / `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS`) already provides the "wins pay more" difference the producer described.

## Existing state

- `buy()` in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` spends the price and adds the entry to the owned set, but deliberately does **not** equip it.
- `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` in `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` clone the payload and currently **preserve** `hangar.activeHull` and `hangar.activeLoadout`.
- `HangarWarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) already carries the deployed `hullId`, `startingWeapons`, `modifiers` and the carried war `payload`, so the scene has the ship identity at battle end.
- `parseHangar` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) restores `activeHull` / `activeLoadout`; `createDefaultPayload` seeds the starter hull and starter weapon as owned, not equipped.
- Permanent levels live in `hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels`.
- Precedent: `resolveHexCapture` already derives the hex's defending bot from the deployed hull (`leaveDefender`), so "the flown hull is spent" fits the existing capture model.

## Desired change

- Add a **pure consumption reducer** (for example `consumeDeployedShip(hangar, ship, catalogue)`) that removes the flown hull, equipped starting weapons and modifiers plus their level rows, resets `activeHull` to the starter hull and clears `activeLoadout`, and preserves the starter kit and every un-flown owned item.
- Apply it on **both** the win path (`resolveHexCapture`) and the loss path (`resolveDeploymentDefeat`), driven by the deployment's hull and the hangar's active loadout.
- Add **auto-enable on purchase** to the hangar purchase path (`purchaseHangarEntry` / `buy` with an explicit `equipOnPurchase` option), keeping `buy`'s default non-equipping behaviour for other callers.
- Update the hangar screen so a purchase reads as equipped immediately, and update the affected unit/integration tests and docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — add the pure `consumeDeployedShip` reducer and an `equipOnPurchase` option on `buy`; keep the default non-equipping for other callers.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — consume on the `resolveHexCapture` win path and the `resolveDeploymentDefeat` loss path; thread the deployed ship into both.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — expose the exact equipped set (hull + active loadout) that consumption applies to.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the deployment's hull/loadout into the capture and defeat resolvers.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `purchaseHangarEntry` uses `equipOnPurchase` and renders the auto-equipped state immediately.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — persist the auto-equipped purchase through the same payload write.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — confirm the consumed/auto-equipped payload round-trips; no schema bump expected.
- Tests beside each module plus the `hangarWarFlow` integration test.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Economy treadmill.** Consuming the flown ship every battle could feel punitive, especially after a loss. Mitigation: wins pay more salvage (existing bonus), and the saved-configuration follow-on (AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7) makes re-fitting one action; validate against the ring-timing budgets before advancing.
- **Soft-lock.** Consumption must never remove the starter kit or leave no deployable ship. Mitigation: always retain `hull-1` and `spread`, and keep the empty-loadout rule (AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D); test it.
- **Silent loss of un-flown levels.** Removing level rows must target only the deployed ids. Mitigation: consume the resolved deployed ids only, and assert un-flown `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` rows survive.
- **Split writes.** Consumption, banking and the win bonus must land in one `saveHangarWarPayload` write. Mitigation: pure reducer plus a single persist, with a test that the balance and ownership cannot diverge.
- **Demo leakage.** An attract/demo run must never consume the player's war. Mitigation: the existing demo guard on `_saveHangarWarPayload`; test it.
- **Scope creep.** Auto-enable could grow into a full loadout-preset system; that is deliberately split into AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7. Price, win-bonus and ring-economy tuning stay out of scope.
- **Stale loadout references.** A save whose active loadout names items no longer owned is already filtered by `resolveActiveLoadout`; consumption must operate on resolved ids, not raw stored ids.

**Assumptions:** both outcomes consume the ship (Q2 = B); only deployed items are consumed (Q4 = B); the ring-end hangar-falls reset is unchanged; and "the ship" is the hangar's active loadout as shown, not the six-slot post-cap run set.

# Pre-emptive counter-push: defuse a pending frontier attack by deploying at its origin

Discovered from: the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 2 of 10; direction: create, **Low** priority — it depends on two sibling items).

## Goal (user story)

As a Hangar War player facing a queued attack on a hex I hold, I want to see that
attack before I deploy and to be able to strike its origin hex instead of waiting
to be hit, so that defending my ring is a decision I make rather than a report I
read afterwards.

## Problem statement

The between-sortie frontier tick resolves **at** the player. `runFrontierTick`
redistributes aggression, resolves queued `pendingAttacks`, and — when nothing is
queued and the seeded 70 % draw passes — attacks one held hex from its most
aggressive unheld neighbour. The player can only respond *after* the tick: there
is no way to see a pending attack before committing a deployment, and no way to
spend a deployment on pre-empting it. Defence is therefore read, not played.

Two sibling items already deliver the two halves this item sits on top of:

- **Strengthen a hexes defence (AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ)** — spend banked salvage to
  upgrade a held hex's defending bot (the *reinforce* half).
- **Do not attack a hex from a hex the player is attacking (AH-0MWH3A87Z005LLOX)**
  — an attacked hex defends and cannot also strike (the *fairness* half).

What neither delivers is the **choice of tempo**: strike first, or hold and
absorb. That is this item.

Evidence of the gap:

- `HangarWarPayload.pendingAttacks` already exists and is persisted, but the map
  publishes it only after it has resolved (via the rolled-in defence report);
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` has no pre-deployment pending-attack surface.
- `runFrontierTick` resolves queued attacks with no awareness of which hex the
  player has chosen to attack, so a queued attack always lands (subject to the
  defender rating).
- `HangarWarDeployment.hexId` already names the deployment's target, so the
  decision input exists with no new payload field.

## The mechanic (full proposal)

1. **Publish the threat before the commitment.** On the hex map, a queued or
   imminent attack is drawn on the ring **before** the player deploys —
   origin hex, target hex, attacking force, the target defender's rating and the
   resulting margin — using the numbers the report already prints, only earlier.
   The `◀ HANGAR`/deploy flow stays one click.
2. **Deploying at the origin defuses it.** When a deployment whose `hexId` is the
   origin of a queued attack **wins** (its mini-boss is defeated), that queued
   attack is cancelled in the same capture payload write: the target hex is not
   attacked on this tick, and the report names the defusal ("_struck first at
   hex X — the attack on hex Y never launched_"). Losing the deployment changes
   nothing: the attack still resolves, so a failed pre-emption costs exactly a
   run.
3. **A visible trade.** The map states the trade at a glance: the origin's
   aggression, the defender it would leave un-upgraded, and the held hex that
   currently stands to be hit — so "strike first" versus "reinforce and hold" is
   an informed choice, the two being the same salvage in different places.
4. **No new battle model.** Everything stays arithmetic over stored numbers: a
   defusal removes a queued attack record; it never simulates hex-versus-hex
   combat, never adds a live defence, and never changes an existing force,
   aggression multiplier, jitter or margin.
5. **Pure and replayable.** The defusal rule lives in the shared frontier tick
   module as a parameter (`attackingHex`, already threaded by the sibling item),
   so a tick remains a pure function of `(payload, seed, tick, attackingHex)`
   and the same inputs replay identically. The map panel is rendered from the
   same pure intel module the report already uses.

## Why this improves player enjoyment

- It converts the outer loop's most passive moment ("here is what happened to
  you") into an active one ("here is what is about to happen — what will you
  do?").
- It gives a low-salvage player a real counter-play against the frontier
  treadmill that does not require out-buying the aggression budget.
- It makes the ring's two named failure modes — the treadmill and the opaque
  defence — answerable by the player's own sequencing, which is the difference
  between a war and a chore.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The hex map publishes a queued/imminent attack **before** deployment: origin,
   target, attacking force, defender rating and margin, read from the shipped
   pure intel module (no scene-local arithmetic, and no second copy of the
   resolver's formula).
2. A **winning** deployment whose target hex is the origin of a queued attack
   cancels that attack in the same payload write; the target hex's defence is
   not resolved on that tick and the rolled-in report announces the defusal.
3. A **losing** deployment at that origin leaves the queued attack intact and it
   resolves exactly as today.
4. An ordinary deployment (no queued attack at its origin) is byte-identical to
   today's tick: the existing `resolveDefence`, `attackingNeighbour` and
   `runFrontierTick` suites pass unchanged, and the 70 % attack-chance draw order
   is unchanged.
5. Both `PlayScene` tick paths carry the deployment's `hexId` (winning path at
   the mini-boss victory, losing path at the run-end handoff), as established by
   the sibling fairness item; the defusal is decided inside the pure tick, never
   in `PlayScene`.
6. No new persisted field: the decision input is the existing
   `HangarWarDeployment.hexId` and the existing `pendingAttacks`; a save written
   before this change loads and resolves exactly as today.
7. `GymHexWar` can queue an attack, declare the attacking hex and show both the
   pre-deployment threat panel and the defusal outcome through the shipped code
   path, with a row in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
8. Automated tests pin: the pre-deployment panel content, defusal on a win,
   non-defusal on a loss, the no-change regression, both `PlayScene` paths, and
   replay determinism for `(payload, seed, tick, attackingHex)`.
9. Documentation: GDD §8.2 (the capture cycle and the defence report) and the
   new §8.3 entry, plus `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D's
   anti-checklist section.
10. The full project test suite passes (through the test skill).

## Impact

A player can see an incoming attack on the ring before spending a life and can
choose to strike the hex that is about to hit them instead, so holding the ring
becomes a sequence of decisions rather than a bill that arrives after each
sortie.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **Depends on the two siblings.** The reinforcement sink is delivered by
  AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ and the fair-origin rule by AH-0MWH3A87Z005LLOX; this item
  adds only the pre-deployment threat surface and the defusal rule. It must be
  planned after both and must not re-implement either.
- **Arithmetic only.** No simulated battle, no new resolver, no new rating
  formula — the defence comparison is the shipped one.
- **One payload, no new fields.** No schema version bump; field-presence only.
- **Scope discipline.** Out of scope: rebalancing aggression, changing the 70 %
  attack chance, changing which held hex the frontier targets, and any live
  hex-versus-hex combat (there is none).
- **Determinism is a hard requirement** — a defusal may not consume or reorder
  seeded draws for an unchanged attacking hex.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — the defusal rule inside `runFrontierTick`,
  parameterised by the attacking hex.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — the pre-deployment threat panel content.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` / `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — panel render
  and the deploy action.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass `hexId` on both tick paths, and announce the
  defusal on the landing map.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — the parity surface.
- GDD §8.2, §8.3; `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D.

## Related work

- Strengthen a hexes defence (AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ) — dependency (the reinforce
  half of the same choice).
- Do not attack a hex from a hex the player is attacking (AH-0MWH3A87Z005LLOX) —
  dependency (threads the attacking hex and the fair-origin rule).
- Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min vs the authored 40–60 min
  window (AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X) and Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured
  48.1 min vs the authored 90–120 min window (AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5) — a cheaper
  counter-play changes the measured line and both must be re-measured.
- The ring-end hangar assault and the frontier tick (GDD §8.2) — the
  arithmetic-only invariant this item preserves.

# Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action

## Problem statement

When a hex battle ends, the deployed ship is consumed (AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF) and the player must rebuild from salvage, so re-purchasing and re-equipping a known build is repeated busywork. Saved ship configurations let the player store a named build once and re-apply it — purchase plus equip every part — in a single action, then fly.

## Users

- **Primary — the player** who repeatedly flies the same preferred build through the hex war and re-fits it after each sortie.
- **Secondary — the balance/progression owner**, because reducing re-fit friction makes the post-battle economy treadmill tolerable.

Example user stories:

- As a player, I want to save my preferred build by name, so I don't have to remember which hull, weapons and modifiers I fly.
- As a player, I want to select a saved build from a drop-down and have every part purchased and equipped in one action, so re-fitting after a battle takes one click instead of a dozen.
- As a player, I want a saved build I cannot currently afford to tell me exactly what is missing (which entries/minerals/cores), so I know what to earn before I try again.
- As a player, I want to rename or delete saved builds, so the list stays useful as my builds evolve.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Save a named build.** The hangar can capture the currently equipped ship configuration as a named saved build: the equipped hull (`activeHull`), the equipped starting weapons (`activeLoadout.startingWeapons`), the equipped modifiers (`activeLoadout.modifiers`), and the permanent levels that configuration relies on (`hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels` rows for those kinds).
- **One-action purchase and equip.** A drop-down on the hangar screen lists saved builds; selecting one **purchases and equips every upgrade the build needs in one action** — the hull becomes `activeHull`, starting weapons join `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, modifiers join `activeLoadout.modifiers`, and any missing permanent levels are bought — through the existing pure economy/payload updaters, never scene-only logic.
- **Affordable builds apply atomically; unaffordable builds report the shortfall.** A build whose combined salvage cost the player cannot currently afford must report the exact shortfall (which entries, minerals and/or cores are missing) and apply **nothing** — neither partial purchase nor partial equip, and no currency spent.
- **Saved builds can be saved, renamed and deleted.** The hangar surface supports creating a saved build from the current configuration, renaming an existing one, and deleting one, and the list is persisted in the hangar-war payload. **Saved builds survive a war reset** (producer decision): `restartHangarWar` preserves the saved-build list alongside `bestScore`, because saved configurations are a "what you own" meta-layer rather than war progress.
- **Saved builds are unbounded in number, with a delete affordance.** There is no cap on how many saved builds a player may hold (producer decision), so the drop-down list plus the save/rename/delete surface is the only management mechanism — deleting a build must be reachable for every entry.
- **A saved build referencing a now-unavailable entry never breaks.** Selecting a saved build whose parts are not in the catalogue (or are ring-gated) reports the same shortfall/refusal path rather than throwing or silently applying a partial build; the economy's `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence is respected.
- **Automated tests cover the feature through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity).** Saving captures the exact equipped set plus level rows; selecting an affordable build purchases and equips atomically; an unaffordable build reports every missing item/currency and applies nothing; rename/delete round-trip (deletion reachable for every saved build); a saved build missing a catalogue entry refuses safely; `restartHangarWar` keeps the saved-build list while wiping unlocks/levels/loadout; and the payload round-trips through `hangarWarStore` without a schema-version bump (the shape is additive).
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

After a battle you pick your saved build from the hangar drop-down and, if you can afford it, the whole ship is re-purchased and re-equipped in one action — re-fitting becomes one click instead of repeated busywork.

## Constraints

- **Pure core, scene seam.** Purchase, equip and level arithmetic live in the pure economy/payload updaters; the screen and scene only present and persist, so gym↔game parity holds (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **Atomic apply.** A build applies fully or not at all; no partial purchase, no partial equip, no spend on a refused build.
- **Additive payload field.** Saved builds are a new optional field on the hangar payload, migrated by field presence without a schema-version bump (the established pattern for `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` / `frontierTick`), and omitted on write when empty so a save round-trips byte-for-byte.
- **War-reset interaction.** `restartHangarWar` currently calls `createDefaultPayload`, which resets the entire hangar to starters (all unlocks, levels and loadout). The producer decided **saved builds survive a reset**, so `restartHangarWar` must thread `savedBuilds` through beside `bestScore` (other hangar state stays at the reset default).
- **One payload write.** Applying a build persists through the existing `saveHangarWarPayload`; demo/attract runs must never overwrite the player's war (existing demo guard).
- **No soft-lock.** A saved build must never leave the player with no deployable ship; the free starter hull/weapon rules are unchanged.
- **Economy precedence preserved.** A build's parts are validated with the existing `owned → gated → unaffordable` rule; auto-enable on purchase (AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR) is the per-part primitive this feature composes, not a re-implementation.
- **Scope creep risk.** A full loadout-preset/sharing system, cross-device sync, or balance tuning of prices is out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Existing state

- `HangarState` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) holds `activeHull`, `activeLoadout` (starting weapons + modifiers), `unlockedHulls`/`unlockedWeapons`/`ownedModifiers`, and optional `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` rows; it has **no** saved-build field.

- **Scope creep.** A general loadout-preset/sharing system or price/balance tuning could creep in. Mitigation: record extra opportunities as linked work items; keep this item to save/apply/rename/delete + shortfall.
- **Assumptions:** saved builds capture equipped ids plus the level rows they rely on; applying a build validates all parts before spending; demo/attract runs never persist a build application (existing demo guard).

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — pure `buildFromHangar`, `applySavedBuild` (atomic purchase+equip, structured shortfall), reusing `buy`/`buyUpgrade`.

# Owned hexes provide minerals (AH-0MWL8CDGN005878A)

## Problem statement

Holding a hex on the ring currently has no economic payoff between sorties:
the only persistent mineral income is the salvage a run banks at its checkpoint
and the fixed win bonus, so capturing hexes buys safety and loadout grants but
never a stream of minerals. Give each **held** hex a deterministic per-tick
mineral income proportional to its aggression (`10 × aggression` per hex,
summed over the hexes still held after the tick) and bank it into the
persistent hangar balance (`hangar.bankedMinerals`) alongside the existing
salvage, so owning territory compounds into the weapons and upgrades the
player buys.

## Users

- **As a Hangar War player**, I want every hex I hold to pay mineral income each
  between-sortie tick scaled by how hard that hex is to keep, so taking and
  holding high-aggression territory is economically worthwhile and the ring
  reads as an asset, not just a boss list.
- **As a Hangar War player**, I want the income announced when the
  between-sortie report lands, so I can see my holdings paying out rather than
  wondering where the extra minerals came from.
- **As a producer**, I want the income rule to be a single pure, tunable
  arithmetic rule over the ring's held hexes with no saved-field migration, so
  the balance can be retuned by one constant without a schema version bump.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Pure, deterministic income rule.** A new pure rule computes the
  per-tick mineral income as
  `Σ over ring.hexes where held: HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION × aggression`
  (`HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION = 10`, producer Q1). It returns a
  non-negative whole number and consumes **no RNG and no wall clock**. Table
  tests pin the empty ring (`0`), a one-held-hex ring (`10 × aggression`), a
  partially held ring (only held hexes counted), and a fallen hex contributing
  `0`.
- **AC2 — Banked once per between-sortie tick.** One `runFrontierTick` adds the
  AC1 amount to `hangar.bankedMinerals`; a second tick banks again (income is
  per-tick, not one-off), and a demo-mode sortie never persists its income. A
  test proves a single sortie resolves one tick and therefore banks one income
  amount (no double-bank via the win path and `_finishRun`).
- **AC3 — Post-tick snapshot (producer Q2 = b).** Income is computed from the
  ring **after** the tick's aggression redistribution and after the AI attacks
  resolve, counting only hexes still `held` and using their post-tick
  `aggression`. A hex lost during the tick therefore pays nothing for that
  tick. A test drives a tick that loses a held hex and asserts the fallen hex
  contributes `0` while survivors pay `10 × aggression`.
- **AC4 — Tick record and report visibility (producer Q3 = a).**
  `FrontierTickRecord` carries the income (`hexIncome`), and the between-sortie
  report/map renders a `HEX INCOME BANKED: +N MINERALS` line when `N > 0`
  (mirroring the existing `winBonusLine`), with no line when `N = 0`. A test
  asserts the line for a ring with held hexes and its absence for an empty
  ring.
- **AC5 — Gym and headless parity.** `GymHexWar` and the headless evaluation
  arena, which already call `runFrontierTick`, expose the same income in the
  tick record through the shared code path (no gym-local re-derivation), and
  never double-count because a re-render re-runs the pure tick on a retained
  payload. A gym test asserts the record's income matches the game's for the
  same payload.
- **AC6 — Migration and robustness.** No new persisted field is required: a
  save written before this change still ticks, deriving income from its
  current held hexes. Corrupt, negative or non-integer aggression and held
  state normalise safely (`aggression` clamped to a non-negative integer, a
  non-held hex contributes `0`); the banked balance is clamped to a
  non-negative integer on write, and the income never consumes a seeded RNG
  draw (the aggression and attack streams stay byte-identical for the same
  payload/seed/tick).
- **AC7 — Docs and comments.** README (Hangar War / hex map and economy
  sections), the GDD §8.2 economy notes and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
  (Candidate D) describe the income rule and mark the `10 × aggression`
  multiplier a balance knob; the new rule's JSDoc states the formula, the
  post-tick timing decision and the migration behaviour. All related
  documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8 — Test suite.** Focused unit tests cover the pure rule, the tick
  integration, the post-tick ordering case, the no-RNG-draw property and the
  report line; full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Holding territory now pays out every between-sortie tick in proportion to each
hex's aggression, so a player's owned hexes visibly fund the weapons and
upgrades they buy instead of only granting a one-off capture reward.

## Constraints

- **Pure arithmetic only.** The design of record
  (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, Candidate D) requires that between-run
  economy and frontier resolution stay *algorithmic over stored numbers* — no
  simulated economy, no wall clock, no new RNG stream (adding a draw would
  shift the seeded frontier stream and break deterministic replays).
- **Post-tick snapshot (producer Q2 = b).** Income is read from the payload
  *after* redistribution and attacks, so it must be computed at the end of
  `runFrontierTick`, not before.
- **One shared code path.** The game, `GymHexWar` and the headless arena must
  bank/expose income through `runFrontierTick` and one pure rule; no divergent
  copy (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- **No schema break.** The payload is field-presence migrated; the income is
  derived from `ring.hexes[].held` and `ring.hexes[].aggression`, which already
  exist, so no new persisted field and no `version` bump.
- **Balance note.** At `10 × aggression`, a fully held ring 1 (aggression
  total 18) pays `180`/tick, which exceeds the `100` win bonus and the measured
  ~24 minerals per deployment. This is the producer's Q1 choice; the multiplier
  is a single tunable constant and any retune is a one-line change (a
  re-baselining follow-up, not folded into this item).

## Existing state

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `runFrontierTick` is the one
  between-sortie transition: it redistributes aggression, resolves attacks and
  advances `frontierTick`, returning `{ payload, clock, record }`. It does not
  currently touch `hangar.bankedMinerals`. `applyDefence` clears `held` and
  `defender` on a fallen hex but keeps its aggression.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HexState.held` is the ownership flag and
  `HexState.aggression` the per-hex value; `HangarState.bankedMinerals` is the
  persistent balance.
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — `bankSalvage` / `bankWinBonus` bank
  minerals from checkpoint snapshots and the fixed win bonus; the income rule
  is a third, independent source into the same balance.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — `winBonusLine` is the existing
  announcement pattern (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`) the income line
  mirrors.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_resolveBetweenSortieTick` runs the tick once
  per sortie (the win path resolves it before the capture and `_finishRun`
  reuses `pendingBetweenSortieTick`), so banking is naturally per-sortie.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — calls `runFrontierTick` for the map record.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — Candidate D names a "per-tick arithmetic
  rule over the region's holdings" and the algorithmic-resolution constraint.
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` and AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA — the income
  anchor: ~24 minerals mean per ring-1 deployment, ~22.3 per ring-2 grind
  deployment.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure `hexIncome` rule (in `hexDefence.ts` or a small sibling module)
   that sums `HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION × aggression` over the hexes
   still held after the tick, normalising to a non-negative integer and
   consuming no RNG.
2. Call it at the **end** of `runFrontierTick` (after redistribution and
   attacks), adding the result to `next.hangar.bankedMinerals` and exposing it
   on `FrontierTickRecord` as `hexIncome`.
3. Thread the income through the report/map model as a `hexIncomeLine` sibling
   of `winBonusLine`, rendered as `HEX INCOME BANKED: +N MINERALS`.
4. Document the rule and the `10 × aggression` balance knob.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — add the pure income rule and the
  `HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION` constant; apply it at the end of
  `runFrontierTick`; extend `FrontierTickRecord`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts` — pure-rule table tests, tick banking,
  post-tick ordering, fallen-hex contribution and zero-RNG-draw assertions.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — `hexIncomeLine` on the report model.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.test.ts` — line present/absent cases.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — carry the income line through the map
  model.
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — reference only; confirm the third
  income source does not disturb the checkpoint watermark.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` — gym record parity.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md` —
  document the rule and multiplier.
- `src/core/hangarWar/fixtures.ts` — a held-ring fixture if an existing one is
  insufficient.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` (added at plan) — the local
  `FrontierTickRecord` stub factory must gain `hexIncome` for the type to
  compile; its map-overlay assertions cover the threaded line.
- `src/defenceReportRolledInDocs.test.ts` (added at plan) — the existing docs
  guard that pins `WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS` in the GDD; add the income
  line beside it so the docs change cannot silently regress.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** (completed) — Re-baseline salvage, cores and the
  mini-boss reward value per hex deployment. Supplies the per-deployment income
  anchor (~24 / ~22.3 minerals) against which the new rate is judged.
- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** (open) — Win path: suppress the mini-boss wheel and
  bank a fixed post-win bonus on hex wins. The `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` /
  `winBonusLine` pattern this feature mirrors.
- **AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP** — between-sortie frontier tick (the transition that
  hosts the income).
- **AH-0MVUXC118004B4OX** — salvage banking at checkpoint moments (the other
  persistent mineral source).
- **AH-0MWB9V9Q3004HD2P** — strength-budgeted frontier clock (the tick's
  invariants the income must not perturb).
- **AH-0MWH4F375000X08G / AH-0MWJ4ZDXO007VDJS** — hex variety (landmarks,
  contracts, cache payouts) that a future per-hex yield could build on.
- **AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM** (open) — Hex Map Information UX; the natural surface
  for a per-hex income intel line.
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search minerals` and `wl search "owned hex"`
  returned no completed item delivering per-tick income from held hexes, so
  this is net-new work.

## Assumptions

- A1: "each tick" means the existing **between-sortie frontier tick**
  (`runFrontierTick`), not a wall-clock or frame tick — the design of record
  defines the between-run tick as the economy's cadence.
- A2: "owned hexes" means `HexState.held === true` in the current ring; the
  payload stores only the current ring, so income is over that ring.
- A3: Income is minerals only (no cores), matching the win bonus's
  minerals-only rule, because cores are the rarer mini-boss currency.
- A4: The `10 × aggression` multiplier is the producer's Q1 balance choice; it
  is one tunable constant and may be retuned without migration.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-18)

### Planning decision

**No child decomposition.** This is one cohesive, small (Small effort / Medium
risk) vertical slice: a pure rule plus the one call site that already exists,
the report line that mirrors `winBonusLine`, and the docs. Splitting it into
"tests", "rule", "report", "docs" children would produce horizontal layers
that cannot each be delivered end-to-end, which the skill's vertical-slice rule
forbids. The item is therefore planned as a single implementable unit and the
plan below is the ordering inside it.

### Test-first implementation order

1. **Pure-rule tests** in `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts`: empty ring
   `0`, one held hex `10 × aggression`, partially held ring (only held hexes),
   a held hex with aggression `0` contributing `0`, and hostile input
   (negative/`NaN`/non-integer aggression) normalising to a non-negative
   whole number. → verify: the new tests fail against the current module.
2. **`hexIncome(hexes)` rule** in `hexDefence.ts` plus
   `HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION = 10`, exported for the report tests and
   documented with the JSDoc AC1/AC3/AC6 require. → verify: step-1 tests pass;
   the rule calls neither `tickRng` nor `Date`.
3. **Tick integration**: call the rule at the **end** of `runFrontierTick`
   (after `redistribution` is applied to the hexes and after every
   `applyDefence`), add it to `next.hangar.bankedMinerals` through the existing
   `toCount`, and publish it on the record as `hexIncome`. Add the tick tests:
   one tick banks once, a second tick banks again, a hex lost this tick pays
   `0` while survivors pay `10 × aggression`, and two ticks over payloads that
   differ only in `bankedMinerals` return identical `deltas`/`attacks` (the
   no-RNG-draw property). → verify: tick tests pass; still one `runFrontierTick`
   result per sortie (AC2).
4. **Report + map line**: `hexIncomeLine` on `DefenceReportModel`, derived from
   `record.hexIncome` (see clarification C1), threaded through
   `HexMapAttackOverlay` in `hexIntel.ts` and its `QUIET_TICK_RECORD`/
   `FrontierTickRecord` stubs (`hexIncome: 0`). Tests assert the line for a
   held ring and its absence for an empty one, and that the gym's record income
   equals the game's for the same payload. → verify: report, intel and gym
   suites pass.
5. **Docs**: README (Hangar War / hex map-and-economy sections), GDD §8.2
   (`#### The hangar and its economy`, and the `Measured per-deployment income`
   note that should point at the new stream), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   Candidate D; mark `10 × aggression` a balance knob; extend
   `src/defenceReportRolledInDocs.test.ts`. → verify: docs guard tests pass.

### Implementation clarifications (review-stage findings)

- **C1 — `hexIncomeLine` reads the record, not a new option.** `winBonusMinerals`
  is a `BuildDefenceReportOptions` field because the win bonus is banked by the
  *capture* path, outside the tick. Income is banked *inside* the tick, so it
  already travels on `FrontierTickRecord`: `buildDefenceReport` must derive
  `hexIncomeLine` from `toCount(record.hexIncome)` and add **no** new option.
  That keeps gym↔game parity automatic (AC5) and leaves `hexIntel`'s
  `winBonusMinerals` plumbing untouched.
- **C2 — demo mode is already handled.** `PlayScene._saveHangarWarPayload`
  returns before `saveHangarWarPayload` when `this.demoMode` is true, so a demo
  sortie's banked income is never persisted. No demo-specific branch belongs in
  the income rule; AC2's demo clause is satisfied by asserting the payload was
  not persisted, not by branching in `runFrontierTick`.
- **C3 — the win path resolves one tick.** `_resolveHangarWarCapture` stores
  `pendingBetweenSortieTick` and `_finishRunWithPurpose` reuses it, so the
  income is banked exactly once. The test asserts the reuse rather than adding a
  guard in the tick.
- **C4 — a fully held ring raises no attack.** `runFrontierTick` reports no
  attacks on a secured ring (no unheld neighbour to launch from), which is
  exactly the fully-held fixture the income tests need for the `180` check.

### AC coverage

AC1–AC8 are all delivered by this single item; the AC coverage review reports
full coverage (`proceed`) because the item has no children and is not split.

### Estimate

The `effort_and_risk_skill` estimate recorded on this item (Small effort,
Medium risk, expected 5.33 h, recommended 12.83 h) already reflects this scope
and planning adds no children to re-aggregate, so it is retained unchanged
rather than re-posted.

### Open questions

None — Q1–Q3 were answered by the producer on 2026-11-17 (see the Appendix).
The `10 × aggression` rate being far above the ~24-minerals-per-deployment
anchor stays a documented balance note (see Constraints) with any retune as a
separate follow-up, per the producer's Q1 choice.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18 — plan skill session: reviewed the intake brief against the code
  (`runFrontierTick`, `applyDefence`, `buildDefenceReport`,
  `PlayScene._resolveBetweenSortieTick`/`_saveHangarWarPayload`, `hexIntel`
  overlay); confirmed no children are warranted; added the Plan section,
  clarifications C1–C4, two missing key files and the test-first ordering;
  retained the existing effort/risk estimate; advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions

Answers recorded from the producer (2026-11-17, interactive reply on
AH-0MWL8CDGN005878A).

- **Q1 — Income formula and rate.** How many minerals should each held hex
  produce per tick?
  - (a) Flat `1` per held hex per tick — full ring 1 pays `6`/tick, full ring 2
    pays `12`/tick.
  - (b) Ring-scaled `heldHexCount × ringIndex` — full ring 1 pays `6`/tick,
    full ring 2 pays `24`/tick.
  - (c) A flat `5`/tick whenever at least one hex is held, regardless of count.
  - **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer):** `10 × hex aggression` — each held hex pays
    `10 × that hex's aggression`, summed over held hexes. Source: interactive
    reply to this intake session. This supersedes all three drafted options and
    is captured as AC1 and
    `HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION = 10`.

- **Q2 — Timing when a hex falls this tick.** Should a hex that is lost to a
  frontier attack during the same tick still pay income for that tick?
  - (a) Count hexes held **at the start** of the tick (before this tick's
    attacks).
  - (b) Count hexes still held **after** the tick.
  - **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer):** **(b)** — count hexes still held after the tick, so
    a hex lost this tick pays nothing. Source: interactive reply. Captured as
    AC3.

- **Q3 — Visibility.** Should the between-sortie report/map announce the income?
  - (a) Announce it as `HEX INCOME BANKED: +N MINERALS`, mirroring
    `WIN BONUS BANKED`.
  - (b) Bank silently, with no new UI line.
  - **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer):** **(a)** — announce the income line. Source:
    interactive reply. Captured as AC4.

### Research notes

- Searched `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D), the GDD §8.2 economy
  notes, `README.md` and the changelog: the design names a "per-tick arithmetic
  rule over the region's holdings" but fixes no rate, hence the Q1 question.
- Searched the worklog (`wl search minerals`, `wl search "owned hex"`,

Test-first verification slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (hex-battle consumption + equip-on-purchase). The new reducer's own contract test belongs to the reducer item, not here.

## Scope

- New test file(s) under the hangar-war test area (for example `src/core/hangarWar/consumeOnBattleEnd.test.ts` and `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarPurchaseEquip.test.ts`), each test naming the AC it pins.
- Consumption (through `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat`):
  - a win consumes the flown hull, the deployed starting weapons and the deployed modifiers; a loss consumes the same;
  - the free starter hull `hull-1` and starter weapon `spread` survive even when they were deployed;
  - owned items the player did not fly survive (hull, weapon, modifier, and their permanent level rows);
  - the consumed ids' `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows are deleted;

# Goal

As a player, I want one pure, reusable rule that spends exactly the ship I flew, so the hangar can reflect a battle's outcome without any scene owning a copy of the consumption logic.

## Context

Core slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (producer Q4 = B: only the deployed ship is consumed — equipped hull, equipped starting weapons, equipped modifiers and their bought permanent levels; un-flown owned items and the free starter kit survive). Gym↔game parity means this lives in the pure core, never in a scene.

## Scope

- Add `consumeDeployedShip(hangar, ship, catalogue?)` to `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`, beside `equipHull`/`equipLoadout`, with a `DeployedShip` shape (`{ hullId, startingWeapons, modifiers }`) shared with the capture cycle (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`).
- Removes the flown hull from `unlockedHulls` (unless it is the free starter hull `hull-1`), each equipped starting weapon from `unlockedWeapons` (unless it is the free starter weapon `spread`), and each equipped modifier from `ownedModifiers`.
- Deletes only the consumed ids' rows from `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`; every un-flown id's row and the `bankedMinerals` / `bankedCores` balances are untouched.
- Resets `activeHull` to the starter hull and clears `activeLoadout` (both lists empty), so a deployment still builds with only the ship's permanent cannon.
- Pure and total: the input hangar is never mutated, unknown/stale ids are ignored, a repeated call on an already-consumed hangar is idempotent, and no throw is possible from a corrupt save.
- Contract unit tests beside the module: hull/weapon/modifier removal, starter survival, un-flown survival, level-row pruning (both kinds), balance invariance, empty-loadout result, idempotence, purity.

- `consumeDeployedShip` is exported from the hangar economy module (and its types from `types.ts`), documented with a doc comment that names this parent item.
- On a hangar that owns a starter kit plus a bought hull/weapon/modifier with permanent levels, consuming a deployed ship removes exactly the flown ids and their level rows, keeps every other owned id and row, keeps both balances, sets `activeHull` to the starter hull and empties `activeLoadout`.
- Deploying the starter hull and the starter weapon never removes them, and the resulting hangar is still deployable (a deployment payload builds with an empty loadout).
- Calling it twice with the same ship yields the same hangar as calling it once (idempotent), and the caller's hangar object is unchanged after both calls.

The hangar now has one auditable rule for what a sortie costs, so a win and a loss can never spend different amounts of the player's fleet.
