# Goal

As a player, after a hex battle I want the ship I flew to be spent — win or loss — so each sortie is a real commitment and a bad run costs me the ship, not my collection.

## Context

The gameplay slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (producer Q2 = B: a win leaves the hull as the hex's defender and still spends it; a loss destroys it; the difference is economic — a win pays more salvage). Today both resolvers clone the payload and **preserve** the equipped ship, and the defeat path persists nothing at all.

## Scope

- Thread the flown ship into the pure capture cycle: `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` take the deployment's `DeployedShip` (hull + active loadout as flown), falling back to the hangar's own resolved `activeHull` / `resolveActiveLoadout` when a caller passes none.
- Apply `consumeDeployedShip` on the **win** path (`resolveHexCapture`) and the **loss** path (`resolveDeploymentDefeat`), after the salvage settlement/banking so consumption can never change a balance, and after `leaveDefender` so the defending bot still derives from the flown hull.
- A `campaignReset` (ring-end hangar falls, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J) still returns the freshly reset campaign — the reset wins over consumption.
- `PlayScene`: pass `this.hangarWarDeployment`'s hull and loadout into both calls, and make the loss path persist the consumed payload through the existing demo-guarded `_saveHangarWarPayload` so ownership, banking and the win bonus land in **one** write per battle. `_forfeitUnbankedSalvage` currently writes nothing.
- Keep the demo/attract guard intact: an attract run must never write the consumed payload over the player's war.
- Gym↔game parity: the headless seam (`GymHexWar.captureHex` and the pure resolvers) exercises the same code; no scene-only rule.
- Update the module doc comments that state "losing a run never loses the hangar" to the new rule (the flown ship is spent; the hangar and ring otherwise persist).

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a winning deployment the payload has the flown hull (unless starter), flown starting weapons (unless starter), flown modifiers and their level rows removed; `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty; the win bonus and the banked salvage still land; exactly one payload write happens.
- After a losing deployment the same consumption happens and the payload is persisted exactly once through the demo-guarded write; only the salvage earned since the last bank is forfeited, and the balances are otherwise unchanged by consumption.
- Owned items the player did not fly, their permanent level rows and the free starter kit survive both paths; the post-battle hangar is deployable with an empty loadout (no soft-lock).
- A ring-end `campaignReset` outcome is byte-identical to today's reset payload (consumption does not apply on top of the reset).
- Demo mode (`demoMode` true) leaves the stored `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload untouched on both paths.
- The acceptance tests for consumption (parent test item) go green, and the resolver suites (`captureCycle.test.ts`) plus `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` pass.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate are green.

- On completion of a hex deployment — **win or loss** — the deployed ship is removed from the hangar payload: the deployed hull (unless it is the free starter hull), every starting weapon in the hangar's active loadout (unless it is the free starter weapon), every modifier in that loadout, and the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows for those consumed ids are deleted; every owned item the player did not deploy, and the free starter kit, remain owned. (Restated from the parent item.)
- After the consumption the hangar is reset to the free starter kit: `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty, so the next deployment uses only the free starter kit until the player re-purchases; the player's `bankedMinerals` and `bankedCores` are unchanged by consumption (the existing win bonus still applies on a win). (Restated from the parent item.)

- src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts — `resolveHexCapture` (win) and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` (loss) apply the reducer; module/rule doc comments updated
- src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts — win/loss consumption, campaignReset and refusal-path coverage

Every hex battle now costs the ship you flew, so sorties feel like commitments and the salvage you earn is visibly what funds the next ship.

# Goal

As a player, I want a purchase to arm the part immediately, so re-fitting a new ship after a lost sortie takes one action per part instead of buy-then-hunt-for-equip.

## Context

The economy slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (producer Q1 = C refined: "when an upgrade is purchased it is automatically enabled"). Today `buy()` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) documents and implements "buying only grants ownership — equipping stays the deployment selector's job (A5/A6)". This item deliberately supersedes that rule **for the hangar screen only**, while other callers keep the old behaviour through an explicit option.

## Scope

- Add an explicit `equipOnPurchase` option to `buy(hangar, entry, context, options?)`, default **off** so every existing caller (attract/demo decision, tests, gyms) keeps the documented non-equipping behaviour.
- When on and the purchase succeeds: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers` — each deduplicated. A refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership, balance nor loadout.
- `purchaseHangarEntry` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) opts in, so every hangar-screen purchase lands owned **and** equipped in the same payload.
- `HangarScene` persists the auto-equipped payload through the same single `saveHangarWarPayload` write it already uses, and the screen model (`buildHangarScreenModel` / `renderHangarScreen`) shows the purchased row as equipped/subscribed (`EQUIPPED` / `ON`) on the next render without a second render pass or a hint.
- Keep the un-equip toggles (`equipHangarHull`, `toggleHangarWeapon`, `toggleHangarModifier`) available after an auto-equip — the player can always put a part back on the bench.
- Update the doc comments that state the A5/A6 "buying never equips" rule so they name the hangar-screen opt-in.
- Tests: pure `buy` with and without the option, all three entry kinds, every refusal path, `purchaseHangarEntry` payload result, and the screen model rendering the equipped state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buy(..., { equipOnPurchase: true })` equips a purchased hull (`activeHull`), weapon (`activeLoadout.startingWeapons`) and modifier (`activeLoadout.modifiers`), and returns the spent price unchanged from today's behaviour.
- `buy(...)` without the option behaves exactly as today (ownership only) — pinned by a test so the A5/A6 contract cannot silently drift for other callers.
- A refused purchase with `equipOnPurchase: true` leaves ownership, balance and loadout identical to before the call (deep-equal payload).
- `purchaseHangarEntry` equips on success and persists nothing on refusal; the screen model built from the resulting payload renders the row as equipped (`EQUIPPED` / `ON`).
- An auto-equipped part can still be un-equipped through the existing toggle functions, and an empty loadout stays legal.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate are green, and the auto-enable acceptance tests go green.

- A successful hangar purchase **auto-enables** the entry: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, and a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers`; a refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership nor the loadout; this deliberately supersedes the economy's current "buying never equips" rule for the hangar screen, while other callers can keep the old behaviour through an explicit option. (Restated from the parent item.)

# Re-fit the human-style knobs to the calmer competent flight model

## Problem statement

The human-style fit (`src/ai/style/fitting.ts`) maps a recorded player's style
onto the competent bot's knobs, but its knob set and mapping constants predate
the calmer flight model shipped by AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 (wider travel-turn
deadband, tight 0.05 rad aim deadband, turn reversal hysteresis, 30 ms turn
press hold, pass-through collection). Because the fit still models the old
precision-turning governor, its synthetic-human fixed point lands on the wrong
side of the 1-point competence tolerance on 20 of the 32 seed-sweep seeds
(was 14), so the "styled bot is measurably closer without regressing
competence" guarantee has silently weakened.

## Users (example user stories)

- **Producer tuning style matching** — "As a producer, I want the style fit to
  stay competent after the bot's flight feel is deliberately changed, so I do
  not have to hand-re-baseline the evaluation every time the flight model
  improves."
- **Player/promo viewer of the attract demo or teaser** — "As a viewer, I want
  the styled bot to play like the recorded human *and* still fly competently,
  so the demonstration is not undermined by an unfitted governor."
- **Future "play like me" feature owner** — "As the owner of a future style
  feature, I want the fit to model the governor the bot actually flies, so
  adding a flight-model knob does not silently invalidate the fit."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The style fitting is re-run against the current (calmer) flight model and
  the `evaluateStyleMatch` seed sweep returns to at most 16 of 32 regressed
  seeds (the original bound), or the bound is re-justified with the newly
  measured distribution (count and measurement date recorded in both the test
  and the docs).
- The fitted knobs include the aim deadband (`aimAlignmentToleranceRad`): it is
  set by `fitStyle`, appears in `StyleFit.applied`, is clamped to a safe
  envelope, and is co-fitted with the fit's aim-fallibility knobs
  (`humanInput.skill` / `maxAimErrorRad`) so the random aim error can never
  exceed the deadband it is aiming into. Where the fit derives it, the
  derivation is geometrically consistent with the fitted `engagementRange` so
  the calibrated standoff does not reintroduce the standoff deadlock.
- The governor turn knobs introduced by the calmer flight model
  (`alignmentToleranceRad`, `turnHysteresisRad`, `turnPressMinMs`) are fitted
  from the existing cadence/hold features, or explicitly documented as
  deliberately left at the shipped defaults, so the fit models the same
  governor the bot flies.
- `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md` and `docs/EVALUATION.md` record the new fitted
  values and the measurement date: the parameter-fitting table, the
  seed-sweep stability wording and the `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts`
  comment all state the measured closer/regressed counts, the bound and the
  date; the `styleDocs.test.ts` / `evaluationDocs.test.ts` guards still pass.
- Fitting unit tests cover the new knobs: each is applied and recorded in
  `applied`, clamped at both envelope ends, and `enforceSafety` invariants
  (priority order, survival gap) still hold.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (typecheck, build and
  tests via the test skill).

## Impact

Producers and future style-matching work can trust that fitting a human's style
still yields a competent bot after the flight model was deliberately calmed,
and the sweep's regression bound again means what it says instead of being
widened to accommodate an unfitted governor.

## Constraints

- **Baseline dependency (RESOLVED — landed):** the calmer flight model is
  commit c2e3dadd on `origin/dev` and AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 is `completed`
  (stage `in_review`); the `depends-on` edge to it is still recorded. A stale
  local `dev` (df5d3d3c at plan time) does **not** contain it, so the
  implementer must confirm `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` / `turnHysteresisRad` /
  `turnPressMinMs` are present in their worktree before measuring any sweep —
  `implement.py start` fast-forwards local `dev` to `origin/dev`, which is the
  correct baseline. Measuring against a pre-c2e3dadd tree re-fits the wrong
  governor.
- **Safety invariants unchanged:** `enforceSafety` keeps the fixed priority
  order, band separation and the survival-band margin, and the steering
  safety filter (the never-suicide guarantee) is untouched.
- **Purity and determinism:** fitting stays pure (no wall clock, no I/O); the
  same recording and seed always produce a byte-identical `StyleMatchReport`.
- **Bound policy:** prefer restoring the original ≤16/32 bound. If the
  measured distribution genuinely shifted because the fit legitimately
  changes flight feel, re-justify the bound with the measured distribution
  and date rather than silently widening it, and keep the majority-closer
  assertion.
- **No scope creep:** do not change flight behaviour or the governor's shipped
  defaults in this item (that belongs to AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2); the change
  surface is the fit's knob set/constants, its tests and its docs. New
  opportunities go to linked work items, not into this one.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/style/fitting.ts` fits reaction time, thrust-press durations,
  commitment hysteresis, engagement range, prediction horizon, risk knobs and
  the priority-band tilt. It builds `humanInput` from
  `BOT_HUMAN_INPUT_TUNABLES`, so `alignmentToleranceRad` (0.16),
  `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` (0.05), `turnHysteresisRad` (0.25),
  `turnPressMinMs` (30) and `skill` (1) stay at their shipped defaults and
  never appear in `StyleFit.applied`.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` (calmer flight model) computes the effective aim
  deadband as `min(alignmentToleranceRad, aimAlignmentToleranceRad)`; aim
  intents are exempt from the turn hysteresis and the press hold.
- `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts`'s synthetic human iterates `fitStyle` 8×
  over `createCompetentBotBrain`; the calmer-model branch records 20/32
  regressed and pins `regressedCount <= 20`.
- `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md` ("Parameter fitting" table, "Seed-sweep stability"
  section) and `docs/EVALUATION.md` still describe the old knob set and the
  "must not regress competence on more than half" rule, with no measurement
  date.
- The shipped competent bot itself is unchanged by this item: the fit only
  moves knobs for a caller who applies a style.

## Desired change

Extend `fitStyle` to fit the governor's turn/aim knobs (at minimum
`aimAlignmentToleranceRad`, plus `alignmentToleranceRad`,
`turnHysteresisRad`, `turnPressMinMs`), co-fit aim fallibility with the aim
deadband, re-run the 32-seed sweep on the calmer model, and update
`docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` and the evaluation test comment
with the new fitted values, measured distribution and date. Restore the
≤16/32 bound if achievable; otherwise re-justify it with evidence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/style/fitting.ts` — add the governor turn/aim knobs to the fitted
  set, new clamp envelopes, `applied` entries and the aim-skill/deadband
  co-fit.
- `src/ai/style/fitting.test.ts` — assert the new knobs are applied, clamped,
  and that the safety invariants still hold.
- `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts` — re-measure the 32-seed sweep;
  restore/re-justify the regression bound and record the measurement date.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — read-only reference for the governor knob
  semantics and defaults (no behaviour change expected).
- `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md` — parameter-fitting table, seed-sweep stability
  section, measured values and date.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — align the style-sweep regression wording with the
  re-justified bound.
- `src/ai/style/styleDocs.test.ts` — keep the docs guard green (extend it if it
  should assert the new knobs/date).
- `src/ai/eval/evaluationDocs.test.ts` — the EVALUATION.md docs guard; no
  change expected, must stay green (AC4).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** the calmer flight model may not land exactly as the branch
  currently stands (it is awaiting producer re-review), which moves the
  distribution again. **Mitigation:** re-measure after the model lands; record
  the date and counts, and prefer the distribution-stable majority rule over a
  brittle per-seed expectation.
- **Risk:** over-widening the aim deadband hides a real competence loss.
  **Mitigation:** clamp it to a safe envelope tied to the fitted standoff and
  keep the aim-perturbation/deadband invariant tested.
- **Risk:** re-fitting to reduce regressions could be mistaken for re-baselining
  test expectations. **Mitigation:** ACs require either the original bound or
  an evidence-backed re-justification, not a silent widening.
- **Scope-creep risk:** new flight-model knobs appearing mid-work. **Mitigation:**
  record them as linked follow-up work; this item covers the knobs the calmer
  model already introduced.
- **Assumption:** the fit can derive an aim deadband from the existing
  `StyleFeatures` (engagement distance and risk) without adding a new
  human-recording feature; if a dedicated aim-precision feature proves
  necessary, that is a linked follow-up, not scope here.
- **Assumption:** "the fit's aim skill" is the governor's existing
  `humanInput.skill` / `maxAimErrorRad` pair; the fit need not start fitting
  `skill` from a feature, but it must enforce the deadband/error invariant.

## Related work

- AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 — "Bot oscillates too much" (in progress): the calmer
  competent flight model this item re-fits against; the source of the 20/32
  regression.
- AH-0MUY08XXN003NV0I — "Style matching from telemetry" (completed): delivered
  `fitStyle`, `evaluateStyleMatch` and `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md`.
- AH-0MV03PVZI009870X — "Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel
  tweaks" (completed): the distribution-stable sweep precedent this bound
  follows.
- AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A — "Bot is more gentle on the thrusters" (completed):
  prior feel tweak that forced a style re-seed.
- AH-0MVT2W3RS009ZB2X — "Retire the wallMargin tunable" (completed): prior
  fitting-surface change and its docs/test updates.
- AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98 — "Bot rotation skills" (completed): aim
  skill/fallibility knob the aim-deadband co-fit interacts with.
- Repository docs: `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md` (fitting + evaluation contract),
  `docs/EVALUATION.md` (sweep assertions), `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` (competent
  brain and governor).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which flight-model baseline should the re-fit be measured against?" —
  Answer (agent, from repo evidence): the calmer model on branch
  `wl-AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2-bot-oscillates-too-much` (commit c2e3dadd).
  AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 is in progress and awaiting producer re-review, so this
  item is recorded as `Blocked-by: AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2` until the model lands
  on `dev`. Source: `git log --all`, `git worktree list`, parent audit result.
  **Recommended:** measure only once the calmer model is the baseline — a fit
  measured against `dev` re-fits the wrong governor.
- Q: "Restore the original ≤16/32 bound, or re-justify the bound?" — Answer
  (agent, from the item's own AC): prefer restoring ≤16/32; re-justify only if
  the measured distribution shows the shift is legitimate, recording the count
  and date in the test and docs. Source: this work item's acceptance criteria.
  **Recommended:** restore the original bound.
- Q: "How should the aim deadband be fitted, given there is no dedicated
  aim-precision feature?" — Answer (agent assumption, to be validated by the
  implementer): derive `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` from the fitted
  `engagementRange` and the governor's aim-fallibility knobs so the fit stays
  geometrically hittable at its fitted standoff, clamped to a safe envelope;
  no new human feature. Source: `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` aim-deadband `min()`
  semantics and `src/ai/style/fitting.ts` clamps. **Recommended:** derive from
  the fitted standoff and co-fit with `maxAimErrorRad`, not a new feature.
- Q: "Should the new travel-turn knobs also be fitted?" — Answer (agent
  assumption): yes, fit `alignmentToleranceRad`, `turnHysteresisRad` and
  `turnPressMinMs` from the cadence/hold features (or document why they stay
  at defaults), because they are the human-style knobs the title names and the
  fit must model the governor the bot flies. Source: the calmer-model branch's
  `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` knob set. **Recommended:** fit them.
- Duplicate-work check: performed — `wl search` over "style fitting aim
  deadband", "style match evaluation regression" and "regressed seeds style"
  found no completed or open item that already satisfies these acceptance
  criteria. No duplicate.

# Review the per-deployment mineral income after pass-through collection

## Problem statement

The pass-through collection change (AH-0MWL3C9NQ006HMD6, shipped under the parent
AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2) stopped the bot retro-braking onto pickups and U-turning for
a just-passed one. That is the movement the producer asked for, but it also cut
the minerals the bot banks per deployment: ring-1 grind fell from 9.0 to 7.44
minerals per deployment and ring-2 from 6.0 to 2.67, and the ring-2 mini-boss
checkpoint hold halved (18 → 8). Ring-2 capture rate held at 33.3 %, so the bot
still wins the sorties — it is simply leaving minerals on the field.

## Decision (producer-ruled)

- **Q1 = (b) Re-tune collection.** Recover the per-deployment mineral income
  without reintroducing the thruster micro-positioning the producer rejected.
  The missing minerals are being left on the field (the bot still wins the same
  sorties), so this is a collection-routing problem, not a combat one.
- **Q2 = N/A.** The accept-path baseline question does not arise: re-baselining
  happens from the re-tuned bot's measurement, not the current post-pass-through
  figures.

## Users

- **Hangar War players** — per-deployment mineral income is the pace at which the
  unlock tree (hulls, weapons, modifiers) is bought between sorties, so a lower
  income is felt directly as a longer grind.
- **The designer/producer** — owns the trade between the bot's movement
  naturalism and the measured economy.

Example user story: *As a Hangar War player, I want ring-2 sorties to still pay
enough minerals that the next hull is a few evenings away, not two dozen.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Collection is re-tuned** so the bot collects the minerals it currently
  passes without reintroducing precision braking: a distance-/route-aware
  collection (e.g. intercept a pickup ahead, sweep a mineral field/cluster, or
  collect on the way through) rather than chasing each pickup's exact centre.
- **Income recovers.** A fresh seeds-1–3 measurement of the shipped bot shows
  per-deployment minerals at or above the pre-pass-through figures — ring-1
  grind **9.0** and ring-2 grind **6.0**, with the mini-boss checkpoint hold back
  at **18.0** per captured. If no re-tune can reach them without a churn
  regression, the highest achieved figures are recorded, the guard is pinned to
  them and the residual gap is filed as a linked balance item — the measured
  result stands rather than the target being silently restated.
- **Capture rates do not fall** below the post-pass-through baseline (ring-1
  44.4 %, ring-2 33.3 %), and ring-1 recovers toward its 50 % pre-pass-through
  rate.
- **Churn does not regress.** On the same seeded runs the turn-press count, turn
  duty cycle, forward-thrust toggles and reverse presses stay at or below the
  shipped pass-through bot, and reverse presses on collection stay at/near zero
  — the parent's anti-micro-positioning goal is preserved.
- The re-tuned bot's collection change is a tunable-driven behaviour (no magic
  numbers) and any new/changed tunable is surfaced in `tuningFields.ts` /
  GymBotTuning where appropriate.
- The committed income artifact `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` is
  regenerated from the re-tuned bot with `npm run ring-timing -- --one-level
  --income-out docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json`.
- The income guard in `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` and any other pinned
  income/pace values are re-pinned to the regenerated measurement, with the
  reason for each changed pin recorded in a comment.
- GDD §8.2 *Measured per-deployment income (one-level sortie)* — its table,
  verdict and unlock-pace figures — is updated to the regenerated measurement.
- A deterministic guard fails if the committed income artifact diverges from a
  fresh measurement of the shipped bot.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README (if it quotes these figures) and the GDD.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player's between-sortie mineral income recovers to the level the unlock tree
was balanced against, while the bot keeps the smooth, non-micro-positioning
movement the producer asked for — so the next hull or weapon stays a few
evenings away rather than two dozen deployments.

## Constraints

- Preserve the parent's goal: the bot must **not** go back to micro-positioning
  with thrusters. Any re-tune must keep the low-churn movement (turn-press
  count, turn duty cycle, reverse presses) at or below the shipped pass-through
  bot.
- Balance figures are **measured, not guessed** — use the ring-timing harness;
  the artifact is the evidence.
- Prices/drops are **not** changed here; the fix is in collection behaviour, not
  the economy. An economy-side change would be a separate linked item.
- Do not reintroduce precision-seeking braking on pickups to win income back.

## Existing state

- **Shipped change:** pass-through collection is live (commit `783401a2`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` collect behaviour; tunables
  `collectArrivalRadius` / `reverseImminentOvershootGap`; parent
  AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2, child AH-0MWL3C9NQ006HMD6).
- **Pre-change, committed** (`docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json`, seeds 1–3,
  competent bot): ring-1 grind **9.0** minerals/deployment at **50 %** capture
  (18.0 per captured); ring-2 grind **6.0** at **33.3 %** (18.0 per captured).
- **Post-change, measured** (parent's final comment; reproducible from commit
  `c2e3dadd`'s artifact): ring-1 grind **7.44** at **44.4 %** (**16.75** per
  captured); ring-2 grind **2.67** at **33.3 %** (**8.0** per captured). Rush
  lines bank 0 on both rings in both states.
- **Consequence for pace:** ring-2 `hull-2` costs 220 minerals / 3 cores, so the
  mineral-bound pace goes from **37** to **83** deployments on ring-2 income
  (core-bound stays 9). Ring-1 `hull-2` goes from 25 to 30 deployments.
- **Repo is stale:** the committed artifact and GDD §8.2 still describe the
  pre-change bot; the income guard pins `mineralsPerCapturedDeployment` to **18**,
  which the post-change 16.75 fails. Ring-1 capture also moved 50 % → 44.4 %.

## Desired change

Re-tune the collect behaviour so the bot collects the minerals it currently
leaves behind (route-through/cluster-aware/predictive collection) while keeping
the shipped low-churn movement, then regenerate the income artifact and update
its guards and the GDD to the re-tuned measurement.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — the collect behaviour and its target choice.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — new/retuned collect tunables (cluster radius, intercept/overshoot behaviour).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — target selection / overshoot filter, if the cluster-aware choice lives here.
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` — surface any new/retuned tunable in the gym.
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — regenerate from the re-tuned bot.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — re-pin the income and unlock-pace guards.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2 table, verdict and unlock-pace figures.
- `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.ts` / `competentBot.integration.test.ts` — the churn regression gate.
- `README.md` / `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — only if they quote the changed figures.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2** — Bot oscillates too much (parent; pass-through shipped here).
- **AH-0MWL3C9NQ006HMD6** — Overshoot-tolerant approach: pass-through collection and reposition band stop (the change being re-tuned).
- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** — Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment (produced the income artifact + guards).
- **AH-0MVWWGN92008P366** — Review ring 2 aggression floor against the measured builds/losses split (precedent: a producer-decided balance review that recorded options and rulings on the item).
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — the measurement artifact.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — the documented income verdict and pace table.
- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs` — the regeneration CLI (`--one-level --income-out`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — target definition.** The producer chose "re-tune" without naming a
  numeric target; the pre-pass-through figures (9.0 / 6.0, 18.0 per captured) are
  taken as the target because they are what the GDD and unlock-pace table were
  baselined on. If a re-tune cannot reach them without a churn regression, the
  measured ceiling stands and the residual gap becomes a linked item (the
  fallback the ring-2 review AH-0MVWWGN92008P366 used).
- **Assumption:** the post-change figures (7.44/2.67, 44.4 %/33.3 %) reproduce
  from the shipped bot. A fresh harness run is the first implementation step.
- **Risk — re-tuning reopens the audit rejection.** Recovering income could bring
  back precision braking. Mitigation: gate every re-tune on the churn metrics
  staying at or below the shipped bot, and keep reverse presses on collection at
  zero.
- **Risk — small evidence set.** The artifacts use seeds 1–3, so a capture-rate
  move of a deployment or two can be variance; a capture-rate conclusion should
  be confirmed on a wider seed set.
- **Scope-creep risk:** changing prices or mineral drop rates is a separate
  balance item with its own measurement, not something to absorb here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — producer decision (answered 2026-11-18).** After pass-through
  collection, per-deployment minerals fell to 7.44 (ring 1) and 2.67 (ring 2) and
  the ring-2 checkpoint hold halved (18 → 8). Choose: (a) accept and re-baseline;
  (b) re-tune collection to recover income without reintroducing micro-positioning;
  or (c) accept the bot change and compensate on the economy side (separate linked
  item). **Answer (producer): (b) — re-tune collection.** Source: interactive
  reply ("1. b"). The agent's recommended option was also (b), because ring-2
  capture rate is unchanged at 33.3 %, so the missing minerals are left on the
  field rather than unearned.
- **Q2 — baseline confirmation (answered 2026-11-18).** The committed artifact
  records the pre-pass-through 9.0/6.0 at 50 %/33.3 % capture while the shipped
  bot measures 7.44/2.67 at 44.4 %/33.3 %; should the artifact be regenerated to
  the shipped numbers and the `mineralsPerCapturedDeployment = 18` guard
  re-pinned, or does the ring-1 capture drop need its own investigation?
  **Answer (producer): N/A** — with option (b) chosen, re-baselining happens from
  the re-tuned bot's measurement, so the accept-path question does not arise.
  Source: interactive reply ("2. N/A").
## Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT** – Mineral collectable entity and constants (completed)
- **AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ** – Model the per-ring deployment loadout (completed)

# Raise demo upgrade dwell to 2.5 s

**Parent:** AH-0MWL7SU2Q009GEJ2 — Bot selection of upgrades are slower

The attract/demo bot currently picks an upgrade after only 900 ms, so a viewer
has no chance to read the three offers. Raise the dwell to 2.5 s for the
upgrade-selection overlay only, and split the mini-boss wheel's demo spin delay
onto its own constant so the wheel's pace is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Tests: ring generation determinism and invariant contract

## Goal

Write the **failing-first specification** for the seeded hex-ring content
generator (parent AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA) so the generator and grant-economy items
are driven by a pinned, versioned determinism contract rather than by ad-hoc
assertions.

**User story:** As a test/agent, the generated ring is a pure function of
`(seed, ringIndex)`, so I can assert determinism, variety and every design
invariant headlessly — and a change to the draw order fails the suite loudly
instead of silently re-rolling every war.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `src/core/hangarWar/hexRingGeneration.contract.test.ts` pins determinism: for a table of at least 20 seeds × ring indices 1–12, generating twice with the same `(seed, ringIndex)` yields deep-equal hexes (ids, coordinates, boss, strengths, weaknesses, grant, `weaponHex`, `baseAggression`, `isSpecialMission`, `personality`, `contract`, `landmark`), and at least two distinct seeds yield materially different rings (different boss identities and/or grant sets).
- Invariant enforcement is asserted across many seeds and large ring indices (at least 100 seeds × ring indices 1–200): exactly one weapon hex and it is the ring's hardest, exactly one special-mission hex whose grant is a hull catalogue entry, at least one beatable hex (aggression at or below the beatable ceiling), unique ids and coordinates, every coordinate on the ring, and aggression a whole number in `[0, MAX_HEX_AGGRESSION]`.
- A committed golden fixture pins the exact generated hex sequence (id, boss, grant, aggression, flags) for `(seed = 1, ring 1)`, `(seed = 1, ring 2)` and `(seed = 1, ring 3)`, so any change to the draw order fails loudly as a determinism-contract change; the fixture lives in `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringGenerationGolden.ts` and is regenerated only by a deliberate, reviewable act.
- Stream isolation: generating ring 5 for a seed does not change that seed's ring 3 map, and a per-hex draw does not shift its neighbours (per-ring and per-hex derived streams are asserted, mirroring `specialRotationSeed`).
- Purity is asserted: the generator module imports no Phaser, storage or scene module and contains no `Math.random` (static source check), so the map scene and `GymHexWar` share one headless path.
- Unit, property and integration tests cover determinism, distinct-seed variety and invariant enforcement across many seeds and large ring indices.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Red-first convention of this repo:** assertions that cannot be green before
  the generator exists are committed as Vitest `it.fails` (the precedent is
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.hexMiniBossVictory.test.ts` and its paired item
  AH-0MWCOW4IQ003XST5). The generator item turns each `it.fails` back into a
  plain `it`; a leftover `it.fails` fails the suite, so the flip is enforced.
- Assertions must never be weakened to make a red case pass; a red case that
  cannot be expressed this way is recorded as a blocker instead.
- No new production code in this item beyond what a test needs to compile
  (import of the forthcoming generator API may be typed behind a small helper).

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRingGeneration.contract.test.ts` — the new contract/property suite (large ring indices, many seeds, purity and stream isolation).
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.test.ts` — extend with the per-ring/per-hex derived-stream assertions.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.test.ts` — existing model tests; keep green, extend only where the contract belongs with the model.
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringGenerationGolden.ts` — the committed golden fixture of generated rings.

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic).
- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** — origin of `hexRing.ts`, `validateRingDefinitions`
  and the authored rings the contract replaces.
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — per-wave `dynamic` generation modes: the shipped
  precedent for a seeded, reproducible regeneration contract.
- **AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7** — the variety vocabularies (personality, contract,
  landmark) and loud validation the contract asserts.

# Seeded procedural ring content generator

## Goal

Add the runtime **content** generator that replaces the authored ring table:
for any ring index, derive a complete, valid `HexRingDefinition`-shaped ring
from the war's seeded RNG.

**User story:** As a player, every war's hex map is generated from its seed, so
the frontier never stops at the last authored ring and the same seed replays
the same map.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated ring content is a **pure, deterministic function of `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`**: the same seed/ring yields identical hexes (ids, coordinates, boss, strengths/weaknesses, grant, base aggression and variety axes), and at least two distinct seeds yield materially different rings.
- Every generated ring satisfies the shipped design invariants, validated loudly rather than repaired: exactly one weapon hex and it is the ring's hardest, one special-mission hex granting a hull, at least one beatable hex, unique ids and coordinates, and the aggression band/budget rules.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` exposes a per-ring and per-hex derived stream (mirroring `specialRotationSeed`), so a change in one ring or one hex cannot shift another ring's map; no second RNG generator is introduced (draws come from `createHangarWarRng` / `createSeededRng` over `normaliseSeed`).
- The generator is a pure core function in `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` (or a sibling module it exports through) with no Phaser, storage or scene import; `validateRingDefinitions` / `generateRing` stay the validation and ordering seams the generator feeds, and an invalid generated ring throws `HexRingDefinitionError` rather than being repaired.
- Personalities, contracts and landmarks are drawn from the existing bounded vocabularies (`HEX_PERSONALITY_IDS`, `HEX_LANDMARK_IDS`) and shared mechanics only: at most one weapon hex and one special-mission hex per ring, no new combat implementation, and hex ids stay unique within the ring and stable across reloads (`hex-r<ring>-<n>` identity is derived from the same seed and ring index).
- Boss identities are generated from a deterministic, seed-derived identity pool that keeps telemetry traceable (stable for a seed, distinct enough across hexes), and every hex's strengths/weaknesses name real shipped weapon/vocabulary ids.
- The contract tests added by `Tests: ring generation determinism and invariant contract` pass with their `it.fails` markers flipped to plain `it` (no leftover `it.fails` remains).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- **Validation cadence (documented assumption):** the generator validates the
  ring it produced once per generation (a ring open, or a definitions lookup),
  via `validateRingDefinitions`, and throws on any issue. Broad many-seed
  coverage lives in the contract tests rather than in every materialisation.
- **Tutorial variance:** per producer Q1 = B, ring 1 generates from the seed
  like every other ring, so the opening ring varies per war. A fixed tutorial
  ring would be a separate producer decision.
- Draw order is the determinism contract: any later change to field order or
  draw count is a deliberate golden-fixture update, never a silent re-roll.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — the seeded ring-content generator; keep `validateRingDefinitions` / `generateRing` / `ringCoordinates` / `ringSize` pure and reuse them.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` — the per-ring/per-hex derived streams (`ringContentSeed`, per-hex mixing).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts` — boss profile seam the generated identity must resolve through.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts` — `MAX_HEX_AGGRESSION`, `beatableAggressionCeiling`, `hexAggressionLevel`: the aggression band the generator must honour.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `authoredRingBaseMass` / `ringAggressionBudget` / `redistributeAggression`: the budget rules generated rings must satisfy.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRingGeneration.contract.test.ts` — flip the `it.fails` markers and keep the contract green.
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringGenerationGolden.ts` — the pinned golden sequence.

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic).
- **AH-0MWJ4ZDXO007VDJS** — hand-authored ring-1 landmark/contract the generator
  must now derive instead of author.
- **AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH** — ring landmarks (`fortress`, `cache`) the generator
  may assign at most one of each.

# Grant economy with level-scaling repeats

## Goal

Make every grant a generated ring hands out a **real effect**, even when a
large ring needs more grants than the hangar catalogue holds.

**User story:** As a player, every hex promises something real: a new hull or
weapon early, and a genuine weapon/power-up level (or a mineral payout) once I
already own everything — never a silent no-op reward.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Grant economy:** the generator prefers unowned catalogue entries; when a ring exhausts them it cycles level-capable entries and each repeat raises the weapon/power-up level (capped at `MAX_LEVEL`), while unlevellable repeats (hull/modifier) bank a mineral payout; every granted hex resolves to a real effect (never a silent no-op).
- Grant selection is deterministic for `(seed, ringIndex, hex)` and reads the fleet's current owned sets (`weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` / unlocked hulls and modifiers) as an input, so the preference order is reproducible and does not consume an extra draw when nothing is owned.
- `withGrantedEntry` (or the capture seam that calls it) applies the level-scaling repeat rule: a repeat of a level-capable entry writes an effective level row above the base (the shipped `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` "first purchase records 2" convention) capped at `MAX_LEVEL`, instead of only adding an already-owned id.
- An unlevellable repeat (hull or modifier with no level dimension) banks its payout through the shipped banking rule (`bankSalvage` / `salvageBanking.ts`) rather than granting nothing, and a replay of an already-held hex cannot double-count it (the stored held/granted marker guards it).
- A property test over many seeds and ring indices asserts that `resolveHexGrant` returns a non-null result for every generated hex's `grants` id and that the reported `kind` matches the catalogue entry — no generated grant is an unknown id or a silent no-op.
- Unit tests cover: preference for unowned entries; exhaustion then cycling; level raise on a level-capable repeat; cap at `MAX_LEVEL`; mineral payout on an unlevellable repeat; determinism of the chosen grant for a seed.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- **Assumption (documented in the intake and non-blocking):** a repeat of an
  entry with no level dimension (hull/modifier) banks the shipped mineral
  payout instead of levelling. The epic's own acceptance criterion states this,
  so it is implemented as written; a producer correction is a follow-up, not a
  blocker.
- `MAX_LEVEL` is the campaign level cap (10); the repeat rule caps at the same
  value so a deep ring cannot create an uncapped upgrade.
- Scope guard: no new catalogue vocabulary or effect kinds — only assignment
  and level scaling of the shipped entries.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `resolveHexGrant`, `withGrantedEntry`, the capture path that banks contract/cache payouts (the banking precedent to reuse).
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — the shipped banking rule for the unlevellable-repeat payout.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — the grant pool (`hull` / `weapon` / `modifier` entries) the generator draws from.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — the generator's grant assignment (consumes the pool and the owned sets).
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — `MAX_LEVEL` and the level conventions the repeat rule must respect.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` row shapes written by a repeat.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts` — grant application tests.

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic); Q3 = A
  producer decision (cycle real catalogue grants with level scaling).
- **AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU** — buy-to-upgrade: origin of `weaponLevels` /
  `powerUpLevels` and the "effective level above base" convention.
- **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5** — rebalance ring 2's grind budget (open, tangential):
  grant scaling must not reintroduce the grind it tracks.

## Goal

Give every runtime consumer one seed-aware seam for "the definitions of this
ring" and "the definition of this hex id", so no consumer needs the authored
table and a looked-up hex always matches the ring the war is playing.

**User story:** As a test/agent, definition lookup by hex id is derivable from
the same seed as the ring, so intel, the special-mission rotation, the defence
resolver and the harness can never disagree about what a hex is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single pure source seam exists (e.g. `ringDefinitionsFor(seed, ringIndex)` and `findRingDefinition(seed, ringIndex, hexId)` exported alongside the generator) that returns the generated definitions for the war's `payload.seed`; every default currently reading `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` / `hexRingDefinitionsFor` / `findHexRingDefinition` is wired to it.

# On-demand materialisation and an unlimited frontier

## Goal

Remove the authored-successor ceiling from ring progression: opening the next
ring generates it from the seed for **any** ring index, so a war never stalls.

**User story:** As a player, securing a ring always opens the next, bigger ring
— ring 3, ring 4 and beyond — because the successor is generated on demand
rather than waiting for authored data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `materialiseRing` generates the ring from `payload.seed` when the stored ring is empty (a fresh war) and returns a stored ring unchanged when it holds any hexes — never re-rolling, padding or discarding.
- `openNextRing` succeeds for every ring index from 1 upward (asserted through at least ring 10): it generates the successor ring from the seed, appends it to the carried hexes exactly as today, reports `opened: true` and the new `ringIndex`, and no longer leaves the ring secured because an authored successor is missing.
- Ring advancement is exercised end-to-end (secure or rush a ring → next ring opens → its hexes are displayable, capturable and taggable by intel) in an integration test that reaches at least ring 4.
- The aggression budget for a generated ring is derived from that ring's generated base mass (`authoredRingBaseMass` reads the same source as materialisation), so the frontier tick's mass, floor and beatable-hex guarantee hold for rings above 2.
- The `try`/`catch` around a missing authored ring in `createRingState` is replaced by generation for a positive ring index; a non-positive or corrupt ring index still degrades safely rather than throwing mid-render.
- Existing ring-advance behaviour is preserved: a rush past unheld hexes keeps those hexes (held state, defender, aggression) in the payload, and the ring-end hangar assault gate still runs before any advance.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- The stored-ring invariant is absolute: a non-empty `ring.hexes` array is never
  regenerated, so a save's seen map can never change under the player (see the
  save-compatibility item for the defensive-parse half).
- Rush/secure semantics are unchanged: only *where the successor content comes
  from* changes, not when a ring opens.
- This item may keep the authored table present (retirement is the following
  item) but must not require it to exist for progression.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing`, `openNextRing`, `createRingState` call sites and the ring-advance result.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — `createRingState` gains the seed-aware generation path.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `authoredRingBaseMass` / `ringAggressionBudget` feeding off the generated base mass.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts` — ring-advance and materialisation tests.
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/aggressionScenarios.ts` — the harness's synthesised "ring 3+" shape can now use the real generator.
- `src/scenes/hangarWarTraversal.integration.test.ts` — multi-ring traversal integration coverage.

## Goal

Complete the content migration: remove the authored runtime table and the CSV
seeds, and move every scene, fixture, harness and test to the generator —
rings 1 and 2 now generate from the seed like every other ring.

**User story:** As a designer, I no longer author a table per ring; the
generator is the single content source and nothing can drift from it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The authored runtime table `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` seeds are **retired as the runtime content source** (no scene or runtime path imports authored ring content; the CSV parity test is removed or replaced), and rings 1 and 2 generate from the seed like every other ring.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` is deleted or reduced to vocabulary re-exports only (no `HexRingDefinition` rows), `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` are deleted, and `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (the CSV parity test) is removed or replaced by a test that pins the generator as the single source.
- No runtime scene imports authored ring content: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` obtain their definitions from the seed-aware source, and `PlayScene`'s `findHexRingDefinition(hexId)` deployment lookup resolves through it.

- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- **Blast radius is the main risk:** 21 test files and the four scenes import
  the authored symbols today. Migrate by capability, not by symbol-renaming, and
  keep each file's assertions meaningful (do not delete coverage to make the
  build pass).
- The variety coverage that lived in hand-authored ring-1/ring-2 rows
  (personality, contract, fortress landmark) must still be exercised: keep at
  least one variety assertion per axis against a pinned seed that produces it,
  or state explicitly in the item's completion comment why an axis is no longer
  reachable.
- Retirement must not change the `6 × n` geometry or the one-weapon-hex/one-
  special-mission publishing rules.

**Key Files:**

# Save compatibility for generated rings

## Goal

Guarantee that switching the content source to a generator cannot damage an
existing war save: a stored ring is preserved byte-for-byte and a fresh ring
generates.

**User story:** As a player, loading my existing war keeps exactly the map I
have been playing, and starting a war (or opening a ring) gives me a generated
map that survives reload unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Existing saves remain playable and unchanged**: a stored ring (full or partial) is never regenerated or discarded; a fresh/empty ring generates from the seed; defensive parse and migration behaviour is covered by tests.
- A payload written before this change (authored ring hexes, ids `hex-r1-*` / `hex-r2-*`, a stored `frontierTick`, absent `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`) loads and round-trips unchanged: every hex id, coordinate, held state, aggression and defender is byte-for-byte identical after a save/load cycle, with no schema version bump.
- A partial ring (some hexes stored, fewer than the full ring) is preserved exactly and is never padded up to the generated ring's size; the next ring opened is generated from the seed.
- A fresh or empty ring generates from `payload.seed` and round-trips: save → load → the same generated hexes (no re-roll on reload), because generation is a pure function of the persisted seed and ring index.
- Defensive parse behaviour is asserted: a corrupt or absent `seed`, a non-object ring, a malformed hex row and an unknown extra field all degrade to a playable payload (or a clean null) rather than throwing, matching `parseHangarWarPayload`'s existing contract.
- Migration coverage is explicit in tests for: legacy authored payload, fresh payload, partial ring, corrupt ring, and large ring index (e.g. ring 7) round-trip.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- No schema change is intended (producer Q2 = A): the seed and `ring.ringIndex`
  are the only generation inputs and both are already persisted. If an
  implementation detail makes a new field unavoidable, it must be additive,
  optional and migrated by field presence — and that deviation must be recorded
  in the item's completion comment.
- The stored-ring invariant is the safety property: generation may only fill an
  **empty** ring, never rewrite a non-empty one.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `parseHangarWarPayload`, `createDefaultPayload`, `loadHangarWarPayload` / `saveHangarWarPayload` (field-presence migration, no version bump).
- `src/core/hangarWar/storage.ts` — the storage seam the round-trip tests drive.

- `src/core/hangarWar/storage.test.ts` — save/load round-trip tests to extend.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing`'s stored-ring invariant (the behaviour under test).

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic); Q2 = A
  producer decision (pure function of `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on
  demand; only `HexState` persisted).

  additive/optional field-presence migration pattern to follow.
- **AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU** — the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` optional fields

# Saved-build contract and payload persistence

## Goal

Add the persisted saved-build contract — a `SavedShipBuild` row type and the additive `savedBuilds?` field on `HangarState` — parsed and normalised by the versioned store with **no schema-version bump**, following the established field-presence migration pattern (`weaponLevels`, `powerUpLevels`, `frontierTick`).

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (persistence and save model). Today `HangarState` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) has no saved-build field, and `hangarWarStore.ts` normalises every hangar field through a per-field parser.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `SavedShipBuild` is defined in `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` with: `id` (stable, rename-proof), `name` (display), `hullId`, `startingWeapons: string[]`, `modifiers: string[]`, and optional `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows reusing `HangarWeaponLevelRow` / `HangarPowerUpLevelRow`.
- `HangarState.savedBuilds?: SavedShipBuild[]` is additive and optional, documented in the same style as `weaponLevels` (why additive, field-presence migration, omitted when empty).

- Level rows inside a build are normalised through the economy's existing `normalisePermanentLevels`, so a hand-edited save cannot smuggle a non-upgradeable kind or an out-of-range level.

- Unit tests cover every rule above (dropped rows, dedupe, trimming, level clamping, absent field, omitted-on-write).
- Module docblocks record the decision and link this item + the parent.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the `SavedShipBuild` interface and the optional hangar field in `types.ts`.

# Pure capture of the current ship build

## Goal

Add the pure helper that snapshots the currently equipped configuration as a `SavedShipBuild`, so "SAVE CURRENT BUILD" has no scene logic of its own and gym↔game parity holds.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. The economy (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) already owns `resolveActiveHull`, `resolveActiveLoadout`, `hangarPermanentLevels` and `normalisePermanentLevels`; capture must compose them rather than re-derive the equipped set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buildFromHangar(hangar, name, id, catalogue?)` (naming free to adjust, signature documented) returns a `SavedShipBuild` capturing the **resolved** equipped state: `resolveActiveHull` for `hullId`, `resolveActiveLoadout(...).startingWeapons` and `.modifiers` for the loadout.

- `id` is a required input (the caller owns uniqueness) so the helper stays deterministic and side-effect-free — no clock, no randomness, no counter inside the economy.

# Pure atomic apply of a saved build

## Goal

Add the pure reducer that re-purchases and re-equips a saved build in one action: it validates every part first, then applies purchase + equip + level upgrades atomically, or returns a structured shortfall and applies nothing.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**, hardest child. Existing primitives in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`: `canBuy`/`buy` (precedence `owned → gated → unaffordable`), `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` (one level per call, priced from the current level, capped at `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL`), `equipHull`, `equipLoadout`, `findHangarEntry`, `ownsEntry`. The sibling primitive AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR ("auto-enable a purchase") arms a *single* part; a build is many parts that must land together, so the atomicity stays in this reducer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `applySavedBuild(hangar, build, context, catalogue?)` returns a discriminated result: `{ ok: true, hangar, spent }` or `{ ok: false, shortfall, hangar }` where the refused `hangar` is a detached copy of the input (nothing spent, nothing owned, nothing equipped differently).
- Parts are validated before any spend, using the existing `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence per entry; a build whose hull/weapon/modifier is absent from the catalogue reports `unknown`, and one gated by `context.ringIndex` reports `gated`.
- Permanent levels are topped up to the captured level (never down): from the current level to the captured one, applying the same per-level curve `buyUpgrade` uses; a captured level above `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL` is clamped, and a captured level at or below the current level costs nothing.
- On success the hull becomes `activeHull`, the build's starting weapons and modifiers replace the active loadout exactly (through `equipHull`/`equipLoadout`), and the raised level rows are written through `withPermanentLevels`/`buyUpgrade` — spend, ownership, levels and equip all land in one returned hangar.
- The shortfall is structured and complete: the missing catalogue entries (id + kind + `gated`/`unknown`) **and** the exact aggregated mineral/core shortfall, computed over parts *and* level steps, so the UI can name what to earn.
- Atomicity is proven by test: an unaffordable build that would otherwise succeed on its first parts leaves currency, ownership, levels and loadout untouched; a build already fully owned and equipped is a no-op `ok` result that spends nothing.
- Duplicate ids inside a build, an empty name, and an empty loadout are handled without throwing.
- No scene, no persistence and no UI in this child — pure economy only, so gym↔game parity is automatic.

- **Affordable builds apply atomically; unaffordable builds report the shortfall (parent AC this child owns).** A build whose combined salvage cost the player cannot currently afford must report the exact shortfall (which entries, minerals and/or cores are missing) and apply **nothing** — neither partial purchase nor partial equip, and no currency spent.
- **A saved build referencing a now-unavailable entry never breaks (parent AC this child owns).** Selecting a saved build whose parts are not in the catalogue (or are ring-gated) reports the same shortfall/refusal path rather than throwing or silently applying a partial build; the economy's `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence is respected.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the result/shortfall types and `applySavedBuild` beside `buy`/`buyUpgrade` in `hangarEconomy.ts`.
- Dry-run on a scratch hangar: apply `buy` per missing entry (with explicit equip at the end) and `buyUpgrade` per level step; if any step refuses, return the shortfall computed from the refusals and the untouched input.
- Aggregate prices with the existing `HangarPrice` shape; reuse `shortfallFor`-equivalent arithmetic already in the module rather than a second cost model.

## Deliverables

- Pure reducer + exhaustive unit tests (affordable, partially owned, unaffordable, gated, unknown, level top-up, already-satisfied no-op).

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Pure capture of the current ship build** (shares the row shape and the captured-levels semantics).
- Sequences after the per-part primitive AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR where it has landed; if it has not, this reducer owns purchase-plus-equip itself through `buy`/`equipHull`/`equipLoadout` and never a scene-only path.

# Drop-down list of saved builds on the hangar screen

## Goal

Render the saved-build drop-down on the shared hangar screen model: one actionable row per saved build plus the save/manage entry rows, with scrolling when the list overflows, so both `HangarScene` and `GymHangar` show it from the same code.

- `HangarScreenModel` gains a saved-build section (rows plus the focused keys) that is **empty-friendly**: with no saved builds the screen shows a single muted `SAVE CURRENT BUILD` row (or the documented empty-state row) and nothing else changes.

# Name entry keystroke mode for save and rename

## Goal

Add the keyboard text-entry mode the hangar screen needs to name a build — a pure buffer reducer plus the scene's key capture — so saving and renaming never require a prompt/overlay the game does not have.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. The game is keyboard-driven and has no text-entry widget anywhere in `src/`; the hangar screen is a list of focusable rows rendered by `renderHangarScreen`, and `HangarScene` owns screen-level state. Rename therefore needs a small, testable edit mode rather than an OS prompt (which would break gym parity and the no-DOM-testability rule).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pure reducer (e.g. `applyNameEdit(buffer, event)` where the event is `char` / `backspace` / `clear` / `commit` / `cancel`) owning: accepted character set (documented — letters, digits, space, hyphen, underscore), the maximum length shared with the store parser, and trimming on commit; the reducer is total and never mutates its input.
- Commit of a blank/whitespace-only name is refused with a documented reason instead of writing an empty name; cancel always restores the previous name.
- The edit mode is presented as a screen row (`SAVE CURRENT BUILD` / `RENAME` → edit row showing the buffer plus a caret and key hints) built in the model, so `GymHangar` still renders the same screen; nothing about the reducer depends on Phaser.
- `HangarScene` captures printable keys and Backspace only while in edit mode, and the mode leaks nothing: Esc/cancel restores browse mode, the restart confirm and edit mode can never be armed at the same time, and leaving the scene clears the mode.
- Entering edit mode for **save** prefills a deterministic default name (e.g. `BUILD <n>` derived from the current list length, or the hull name) and for **rename** prefills the current name — both asserted in tests.
- Pure tests cover the reducer (typing, max length, backspace at empty, cancel, commit trimming, invalid characters) and model tests cover the edit row; the scene key-capture path is covered through the scene seam test where a scene is already built.

## Goal

Wire apply / save / rename / delete through `HangarScene` so a save/rename/delete/apply each performs exactly one `saveHangarWarPayload` write, respects the demo guard, and restores focus across the rebuild.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. `HangarScene` already has the established wiring shape: a public method per action (`buy`, `upgrade`, `equipHull`, `toggleWeapon`, `toggleModifier`, `restart`) that calls a pure updater, assigns `this.payload` on success, then `persist()` and `rebuildKeepingFocus(key)`. `persist()` is a no-op under demo, so demo/attract runs never overwrite the player's war.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HangarScene` exposes `applySavedBuild(buildId)`, `saveBuild(name)`, `renameBuild(buildId, name)` and `deleteBuild(buildId)`, each returning a boolean ok flag, each calling the pure updater, and each performing at most one `persist()` call (asserted with an injected storage double counting `setItem`).

Part of `Review the per-deployment mineral income after pass-through collection (AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J)` — the implementation slice, producer-ruled **Q1 = (b) re-tune collection**.

# Goal

As a Hangar War player, I want ring-2 sorties to still pay enough minerals that the next hull is a few evenings away, not two dozen, so the unlock tree keeps the pace it was balanced against.

# Target outcome

The collect behaviour recovers the minerals the pass-through bot currently leaves on the field **without** reintroducing precision braking. The missing minerals are left behind (ring-2 capture rate is unchanged at 33.3 %), so this is a collection-routing problem: a distance-/route-aware collection (intercept a pickup ahead, sweep a mineral field/cluster, or collect on the way through) rather than chasing each pickup's exact centre.

Measured recovery target (from the pre-pass-through baseline): ring-1 grind **9.0** minerals/deployment, ring-2 grind **6.0**, mini-boss checkpoint hold **18.0** per captured. Fallback, per the parent's AC: if the ceiling cannot be reached without a churn regression, the highest achieved figures are recorded, the guard is pinned to them, and the residual gap is filed as a linked balance item — the measured result stands.

# Definition of done

- The collection re-tune lands in the collect behaviour and/or target selection, driven by tunables (no magic numbers).
- Any new/changed tunable is surfaced in `tuningFields.ts` (`GymBotTuning`) and the bundled `src/data/bot-tuning.json`.
- The test-first sibling's route-through and churn-ceiling tests pass.
- A fresh seeds-1–3 measurement records the new income and churn, and the recovery/capture results are stated against the target.
- Ring-1 capture rate does not fall below 44.4 % and moves toward 50 %; ring-2 stays ≥ 33.3 %.

# Constraints

- **No thruster micro-positioning.** Keep the pass-through movement: `collectReverseBrake` stays off, reverse presses on collection stay at/near zero, and turn presses / turn duty cycle / forward toggles stay at or below the shipped bot.
- **Collection behaviour only.** Prices, drops and the economy are out of scope (a separate linked balance item if needed).
- **Measured, not guessed.** Use the ring-timing harness; the regenerated artifact is the evidence.

# Risky assumptions

- A route-through/cluster-aware target choice recovers the minerals without a churn regression. If it cannot, the fallback (highest achieved + linked balance item) applies.
- The three-seed evidence set can make a small capture-rate move variance; a capture-rate conclusion is confirmed on a wider seed set if it drives a decision.

- The test-first sibling's route-through, no-precision-braking and churn-ceiling tests pass.

## Impact

A player's between-sortie mineral income recovers to the level the unlock tree was balanced against, while the bot keeps the smooth, non-micro-positioning movement the producer asked for — so the next hull or weapon stays a few evenings away rather than two dozen deployments.

# Speed Up power-up affects weapons only

## Problem statement

The Speed Boost (P5) power-up currently increases **both** the ship's movement speed (thrust and max speed) and its rate of fire by 50 % for 10 seconds. Design intent has changed: Speed Boost should be a **weapons-only** power-up — it must increase rate of fire but leave ship movement untouched. Today an active Speed Boost makes the ship harder to control (faster drift/top speed), which is not the intended effect.

## Users

- **Player** — when collecting a Speed Boost (P5), expects faster firing for the duration, with the ship handling exactly as normal.
  - *"As a player, when I collect a Speed Boost I want my weapons to fire faster, but my ship to handle exactly as it does without the power-up."*
- **Game designer / producer** — expects the GDD, power-up descriptions and README to describe P5 as a fire-rate boost only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — With P5 active, the player ship's **movement is unchanged**: thrust and max speed equal the un-boosted values in the playable game (`PlayScene`) and in every gym. `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` and `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` no longer exist (removed, not left returning 1).
- **AC2** — With P5 active, the player's **rate of fire still increases by 50 %** (effective 1.5 × fire rate) for the level-resolved duration, applied live every frame through the single shared `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer` step (so the game and all gyms inherit it); re-collect refreshes the full duration (never additive), expiry returns the rate to normal, and the boost survives respawn.
- **AC3** — `EffectsRegistry.fireRateMultiplier()` is the **single authority** for the P5 multiplier, reading the level-resolved catalogue stat directly (it no longer delegates to a removed movement accessor); the multiplier value and duration are unchanged.
- **AC4** — **Documentation updated:** the GDD P5 row says the Speed Boost increases **rate of fire** (not movement), and the `types.ts` description, `effects.ts`/`powerUpLevels.ts` doc comments/labels, README references and gym doc comments are updated to match. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship skill release pipeline.)
- **AC5** — **Test cleanup and coverage:** existing tests that assert the P5 movement boost are removed/renamed (not silently left asserting removed behaviour); the fire-rate assertions are retained and strengthened; a regression test proves movement (thrust/max speed) is identical with P5 active while fire rate is boosted; parity/equivalence tests are updated to the new API.
- **AC6** — **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Speed Boost becomes a clean weapons-only power-up: players get faster fire without the ship suddenly handling differently, so the effect is predictable and no longer punishes movement control.

## Constraints

- P5 duration (level-resolved 10 s → 20 s) and multiplier value (1.5 × at level 0, cap 2.5 ×) must not change; only the movement axis is removed.
- The registry module must stay engine-agnostic (no Phaser imports).
- Gym parity principle: the game and every gym consume the same shared `_tickPlayer` step, so the change must not fork gym behaviour (`AGENTS.md` gym-parity rule).
- Hull run-stat speed scaling (`scaleShipConfigForHull`) is **not** part of P5 and must keep working — those deployments scale the base ship config, not `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- No new balance config value is needed.

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) returns the level-resolved `speed_boost` `speedMultiplier` stat (1.5 at level 0) while active, else 1.
- `EffectsRegistry.fireRateMultiplier()` currently simply returns `this.speedMultiplier()`.
- `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) applies both each frame:
  `player.setSpeedMultiplier(registry.speedMultiplier()); player.setFireRateMultiplier(registry.fireRateMultiplier());`
- `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (`src/entities/Player.ts`) stores `_speedMultiplier` and re-derives `_config` from `_baseConfig` via `_applySpeedMultiplier()`. It is called only from `_tickPlayer` (plus `setConfig` calls `_applySpeedMultiplier`).
- Hull speed scaling uses `scaleShipConfigForHull` (`src/core/hangarWar/hullSpeed.ts`), applied to the base `ShipConfig` at deployment — it does **not** call `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- P5 is documented as movement + fire rate in: GDD §4.4 P5 row (`docs/Game Design Document.md` line ~1266), `src/powerups/types.ts` `speed_boost.description`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` label/rationale, `src/powerups/effects.ts` module doc, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` module doc, README (shared combat core, effects registry, gym entries), and `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` doc.
- Tests asserting the removed movement accessor (`EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()`): `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` (the `speed_boost: (r) => r.speedMultiplier()` probe map). Fire-rate-only assertions that must be kept and strengthened (they already call `fireRateMultiplier()`, so they need no accessor change): `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`. No test calls `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` directly (verified repo-wide), so no test needs updating for that removal.

## Desired change

1. **Remove** `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` and make `fireRateMultiplier()` read `stats('speed_boost').speedMultiplier ?? 1` directly while `speed_boost` is active (still a single authority for the fire-rate axis).
2. **Remove** the `player.setSpeedMultiplier(registry.speedMultiplier())` call from `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer`, leaving only `setFireRateMultiplier(...)`.
3. **Remove** `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (and its now-dead `_speedMultiplier` / `_applySpeedMultiplier` support), folding the plain config assignment into `setConfig`; update the `Player._baseConfig` doc comment.
4. **Update docs/descriptions:** GDD P5 row, `types.ts` description, `powerUpLevels.ts` label/description/rationale, `effects.ts` module/roadmap comments, README references, `GymPowerUpsUtility`/`GymPlayer`/`hullSpeed`/`hangarDeployment` doc comments — all to describe P5 as a fire-rate (weapons-only) boost.
5. **Clean up tests:** delete/replace movement-boost assertions; keep and strengthen fire-rate assertions; add a regression test that movement (thrust/max speed) is identical with P5 active while fire rate is 1.5 ×.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — remove `speedMultiplier()`; have `fireRateMultiplier()` read the catalogue stat directly; update module doc.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — remove the `setSpeedMultiplier(...)` call from `_tickPlayer`; update the step doc/comment.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — remove `setSpeedMultiplier()` and its dead `_speedMultiplier`/`_applySpeedMultiplier` support; simplify `setConfig`; update `_baseConfig` doc.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — change `speed_boost.description` to a rate-of-fire-only description.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — update the `speed_boost` `speedMultiplier` spec label/description/rationale to fire-rate wording.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the P5 row and related references.
- `README.md` — update shared-core / effects-registry / gym references that mention movement + fire rate.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — update the module doc (Speed Boost bullet + `setSpeedMultiplier` reference).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — update the "live Speed Boost multipliers" doc wording.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hullSpeed.ts` — update the doc comment that references `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — update the doc comment that references `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB** — "Speed power up should increase all speeds" (completed, shipped v0.1.6). This item **reverses** its movement-axis half: it added "all speeds" (movement + rate of fire); the new intent keeps only the weapon rate-of-fire half.
- **AH-0MU8QURXB008DWM7** — "PlayScene: apply P5 Speed Boost multiplier live" (completed). Added the original movement-only application; its movement half is now retired.
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** — "Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9)" (completed). Catalogue/effects foundation.
- **AH-0MTCNYWDO007B6CJ** — "Unit tests: power-up effects, refresh & magnet math" (completed). Test foundation to be cleaned up.
- **AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC** — "Temporary upgrades should always be temporary" (completed). Preserves re-collect/expiry semantics referenced by AC2.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S** – Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement (completed)
- **AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V** – Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship (completed)
